title: Stale cancelSession() from an aborted begin task can kill the NEXT dictation session
description: The begin task's abort paths (lines 1270, 1318, 1327) and handleCaptureFailure (line 1357: `Task { await engine.cancelSession() }`) call `engine.cancelSession()` with no session-generation guard on the engine side. cancelSession (Sources/Talkie/TranscriptionEngine.swift:579) unconditionally finishes the input continuation, cancels the analyzer/resultsTask, and clears handlers. Rapid start/stop sequence: press→release (fast tap, endDictation's `guard sessionLive else` path)→press again. Task1's `beginSession(1)` is still in flight; Task2's `beginSession(2)` is enqueued on the engine actor. When beginSession(1) completes, Task1's guard fails (`self.sessionID == myID` is stale) and it enqueues cancelSession — which can run AFTER beginSession(2) has set up the new session, destroying it. Task2 then resumes, its guards pass (isDictating true, sessionID==2), and it starts audio into a finished continuation: the user speaks into a dead session and gets an empty transcript with no error.
proposed_fix: Give TranscriptionEngine a per-session generation token: beginSession increments and returns it (or stores it), and add cancelSession(generation:)/finishSession(generation:) overloads that no-op when the token doesn't match the current session. Route all stale-abort call sites in AppDelegate (1270, 1318, 1327, 1357) through the token captured when THAT task's session was created. Alternatively, on the engine actor, have cancelSession only act when the analyzer instance it captured at call-scheduling time is still the current one.
verifier_notes: [real/high] Confirmed by reading the code. TranscriptionEngine (Sources/Talkie/TranscriptionEngine.swift:73, an actor) has no session-generation token: cancelSession() (line 579) unconditionally finishes inputContinuation, cancels analyzer/resultsTask, and clears all handlers ("inputContinuation?.finish() ... analyzer = nil; transcriber = nil"), and beginSession (line 347) carries no generation either. In AppDelegate.swift, the begin task's stale-session abort paths (lines 1268-1270 and 1316-1318: "guard self.isDictating, self.sessionID == myID else { streaming?.cancel(); await engine.cancelSession()") and handleCaptureFailure (line 1357: "Task { await engine.cancelSession() }") all issue engine-wide cancels. The claimed race is reachable: endDictation's fast-tap path (line 1386 guard sessionLive) only resets UI (sessionID += 1 exists solely at line 1031), so press->quick release->press leaves Task1 suspended inside beginSession(1) (slow awaits: resolvedLocale, ensureModelInstalled, analyzer.start) while Task2 enqueues beginSession(2) on the same actor. When beginSession(1) returns, Task1's guard fails and enqueues cancelSession, which via actor reentrancy can run after beginSession(2) has assigned inputContinuation/analyzer (set synchronously at lines 386-389, then suspends at analyzer.setContext/analyzer.start) or after it returns — destroying session 2. Task2's MainActor guard then passes (isDictating true, sessionID==2), audio.start feeds the already-finished continuation (yields silently dropped), sessionLive=true, HUD shows listening; at stop finishSessionDetailed finds analyzer/resultsTask nil and returns an empty transcript with no error. The benign ordering (cancel lands before beginSession(2)) also exists, so it is a true scheduling race. Not covered by any known-deliberate decision. Severity: real silent data loss of one dictation, but needs rapid press-release-press with setup still in flight plus adverse actor scheduling, and self-heals next session — medium, not high/critical. Fix direction: engine-side session generation checked in cancelSession, or cancel via the session handle rather than engine-wide. | [real/high] CONFIRMED by reproduction walk-through. (1) engine.cancelSession (Sources/Talkie/TranscriptionEngine.swift:579) has no session-generation guard — unconditionally does `inputContinuation?.finish(); analyzer.cancelAndFinishNow(); resultsTask?.cancel()` and clears handlers. (2) The rapid press→release→press sequence is reachable: endDictation's abandoned-setup path (AppDelegate.swift:1386 `guard sessionLive else`) returns WITHOUT setting isProcessing (set only at line 1418), so beginDictation's guards (`!isDictating`, `!isProcessing`, lines 997/1001) pass immediately on re-press; sessionID increments to 2 (line 1031). (3) When beginSession(1) returns, Task1's guard at line 1268 fails and it enqueues `await engine.cancelSession()` (line 1270) — unordered on `actor TranscriptionEngine` (TranscriptionEngine.swift:73) relative to Task2's beginSession(2), which has multiple reentrancy suspension points (lines 375–436). The engine's exclusivity teardown (lines 356–364) protects against a lingering OLD session, not a LATE-arriving stale cancel. (4) If the stale cancel lands after beginSession(2) installs continuation/analyzer (lines 386–389), Task2's MainActor guard still passes (checks only isDictating/sessionID), audio.start (line 1274) feeds the finished continuation (yields silently dropped), sessionLive=true, HUD shows listening; at stop, finishSessionDetailed returns empty → AppDelegate.swift:1836 empty-transcript guard → hud.hide() with no error. Sibling unguarded call sites confirmed at lines 1318, 1327, and handleCaptureFailure's detached `Task { await engine.cancelSession() }` (line 1357). Severity tempered to medium: the old tap-tap lock gesture was replaced by hold-to-latch (ActivationGesture.swift:17), so the trigger is an accidental quick tap + immediate re-press within the setup window PLUS an adverse actor-scheduling order; impact is one silently lost utterance, recoverable by retry. Fix direction: pass a generation token to beginSession/cancelSession (engine-side guard), or serialize begin/cancel through a single owner task.

title: Dictation press during the ~1s post-insert verification window is silently swallowed
description: In the `.inserted` branch, `await InsertionVerifier.verify(inserted: finalText)` runs inside the endDictation Task, before the `defer { self.isProcessing = false }` releases the latch. InsertionVerifier polls 4×250ms (Sources/Talkie/InsertionVerifier.swift:47-50) and only early-exits when the text is positively found — in AX-unreadable apps (VS Code integrated terminal, Slack, Electron: exactly the heavy dictation targets) all 4 polls run, so isProcessing stays true ~1s after every paste. A new press in that window hits `guard !isProcessing else { hud.nudgeBusy(); return }` (line 1001), and nudgeBusy is a no-op because the HUD phase has already left `.processing` (HUD.swift:427 `guard model.phase == .processing`). The gesture machine still thinks a session started, so the user speaks into nothing, the release is a no-op, and the whole utterance is lost with zero feedback.
evidence: let verdict = await InsertionVerifier.verify(inserted: finalText)
proposed_fix: Release the isProcessing latch before the verification/heal step: set `self.isProcessing = false` immediately after the insert outcome is handled (or move the verify+heal+learn-watcher block into a separate follow-up Task that does not hold isProcessing). Keep the existing internal ordering (verify completes before learning.beginWatching) inside that follow-up task. Also make nudgeBusy fire for the `.inserting` phase, so a press during any residual busy window gets visible feedback.
verifier_notes: [real/high] Confirmed end-to-end. (1) Sources/Talkie/AppDelegate.swift:1573-1577 — endDictation's pipeline Task releases the latch only via `defer { self.isProcessing = false }` at Task exit; the `.inserted` branch's `await InsertionVerifier.verify(inserted: finalText)` (line 2355) runs inside that Task before the defer, so isProcessing stays true throughout verification. (2) Sources/Talkie/InsertionVerifier.swift:47-50,60-74 — 4 polls x 250ms, sleep-before-read, early exit ONLY on a positive looseContains match; `.unreadable` reads keep polling, so AX-unreadable fields always pay the full ~1s. The verifier's own header (lines 10-12) states AX reads false-negative on Electron/web apps (VS Code, Slack, Chrome, ChatGPT). (3) The verify path fires exactly in those apps: AppDelegate.swift:2350 gates on `mode == .paste, optimistic == nil`, and optimistic insertion (1657-1667) gates on TextInjector.focusIsInPlaceReplaceable(), which fails in Electron/web fields per its own comment — so optimistic==nil there. (4) Silent swallow confirmed: AppDelegate.swift:1001-1003 `guard !isProcessing else { hud.nudgeBusy(); return }`, but hud.showInserting was already called at 2328 (phase -> .inserting, hidden 0.4s later) BEFORE the verify, and HUD.swift:426-429 `guard model.phase == .processing else { return }` makes nudgeBusy a provable no-op in this window. (5) Utterance loss: the swallowed .begin leaves isDictating==false; key release yields .end (AppDelegate.swift:707-708) and endDictation's `guard isDictating else { return }` (1367-1368) silently drops it. Not covered by any known-deliberate rule — the 2348-2349 comment deliberately serializes verify vs learn-watcher AX polling but says nothing about holding the isProcessing latch or the silent nudge; nudgeBusy exists precisely to acknowledge busy presses. (InsertionVerifier's "intentionally NOT wired into the insert path" header comment is stale — it IS wired in at 2355.) Severity: real utterance loss with zero feedback, but the window is ~1.0-1.05s per paste, only for paste-mode non-optimistic insertions into AX-unreadable targets, self-healing when the Task exits, and the user gets an indirect cue (no listening pill appears) — medium, not critical. Fix directions: release isProcessing (or a dedicated verify-phase flag) before the verify await, run the heal check detached, or make nudgeBusy acknowledge any visible-or-recent phase.

title: AudioCapture.start() leaves the mic tap installed if engine.start() throws — next session crashes on double tap install
description: `start()` calls `try installAndStart()` with no cleanup on failure. Inside installAndStart, the tap is installed (line 223) BEFORE `try engine.start()` (line 244). If engine.start() throws (transient device flake, device vanished between prepare and start), the error propagates to beginDictation's catch, isRunning stays false, and `stop()` early-returns (`guard isRunning else { return }`, line 345) — so the stale tap is never removed. The next dictation calls start() → installAndStart() → `inputNode.installTap(onBus: 0, ...)` on a bus that already has a tap, which raises an Objective-C NSException (AVAudioEngine's 'required condition is false: nullptr == Tap()') that Swift cannot catch → app crash. The config-change recovery path does this correctly (removeTap+stop in its catch at lines 291-292); start() lacks the symmetric cleanup.
evidence: try installAndStart()  // start(); installAndStart installs the tap at line 223, then `try engine.start()` at line 244 can throw
proposed_fix: In start(), wrap installAndStart in do/catch and on failure mirror handleConfigurationChange's cleanup: `engine.inputNode.removeTap(onBus: 0); engine.stop()` before rethrowing. Alternatively (belt and braces) call `removeTap(onBus: 0)` unconditionally at the top of installAndStart before installing, which is safe when no tap exists.
verifier_notes: [real/high] Confirmed by reading Sources/Talkie/AudioCapture.swift. start() (line 155) calls `try installAndStart()` with no cleanup on throw. installAndStart installs the bus-0 tap at line 223 BEFORE `try engine.start()` at line 244, so an engine.start() failure leaves the tap orphaned. isRunning is only set true at line 173 (after success), and both stop() (line 345, `guard isRunning else { return }`) and handleConfigurationChange() (line 255) early-return when isRunning is false — plus the config observer is only registered after installAndStart succeeds — so no code path ever removes the stale tap. The caller's catch (AppDelegate.swift:1312-1331) never touches audio cleanup either. The next start() passes `guard !isRunning`, reaches installTap on the already-tapped bus, and AVFoundation raises the uncatchable ObjC NSException 'required condition is false: nullptr == Tap()' — app crash. The asymmetry is real: handleConfigurationChange's catch does removeTap+engine.stop (lines 291-292); start() lacks it. MeetingRecorder.swift:144 shares the same AudioCapture class and exposure. Not covered by any known-deliberate decision. Severity note: trigger requires a transient engine.start() failure first (mic seized/device flake), so it is a crash-on-next-use bug rather than an every-run crash — high, not critical. | [real/high] CONFIRMED by reading Sources/Talkie/AudioCapture.swift and the caller in Sources/Talkie/AppDelegate.swift. Reproduction walk: (1) AppDelegate holds one long-lived instance ("private let audio = AudioCapture()", AppDelegate.swift:85), so the same AVAudioEngine/inputNode is reused across dictation sessions. (2) start() calls "try installAndStart()" (AudioCapture.swift:155) with no catch; inside installAndStart the tap is installed at line 223 ("inputNode.installTap(onBus: 0, bufferSize: 4096, ...)") BEFORE "try engine.start()" at line 244. If engine.start() throws (all earlier throws — noInputDevice:193, format guard:208, converter guard:213 — happen before the tap, so line 244 is the only gap), the error propagates out of start() before configObserver registration (163) and before "isRunning = true" (173). The tap stays installed. (3) beginDictation's catch (AppDelegate.swift:1312–1331) does no audio cleanup, and even paths that do call audio.stop() (1348, 1414) are neutered: stop() begins "guard isRunning else { return }" (AudioCapture.swift:345), so removeTap at 347 never runs. grep confirms removeTap exists ONLY at AudioCapture.swift:275, 291, 347 — no caller or other path can clear it, and no config observer is registered on the failed-start path to rescue it. (4) Next dictation: start() passes "guard !isRunning" (130) → installAndStart() → installTap on bus 0 which already has a tap → AVFoundation raises the well-known NSInternalInconsistencyException ("required condition is false: nullptr == Tap()"), an ObjC exception Swift error handling cannot catch → hard crash. The asymmetry claim is also accurate: handleConfigurationChange's catch does the correct cleanup ("engine.inputNode.removeTap(onBus: 0); engine.stop()", lines 291–292) — start() lacks the symmetric removeTap/stop on installAndStart failure. Fix is small: wrap "try installAndStart()" in start() with a catch that does removeTap+engine.stop() before rethrowing.

title: beginSession's exclusivity teardown cancels the old resultsTask without awaiting it — a stale segment can leak into the new session
description: When beginSession finds a lingering session (`analyzer != nil`, line 356), it cancels the old resultsTask (line 360) but never awaits its completion. If the old results loop had already dequeued a finalized result and is suspended waiting for the actor to run `await self.ingest(...)`, cancellation does not stop that pending call. beginSession then resets accumulators and installs the NEW session's onSegment handler (lines 367-373) before suspending at `try await resolvedLocale()` (line 375) — at which point the stale ingest runs against the NEW session's state: previous-session text is appended to the fresh finalizedText/finalizedSegments and delivered to the new session's segment handler (StreamingCleanup), so old words get cleaned and inserted with the new dictation. Triggerable via the same rapid start/stop interleavings as the cancelSession race.
proposed_fix: After `resultsTask?.cancel()`, await the old task's completion before resetting state: capture it into a local, `_ = await old?.value`, then nil it out and proceed with the accumulator reset. Alternatively stamp each session with a token and have ingest() drop results whose captured token doesn't match the current session's.

title: Self-healing retype fires into whichever app is focused after the ~1s verify — can type the transcript into the wrong app
description: The B2 heal path verifies the paste by polling the CURRENT focused field (InsertionVerifier reads AXFieldReader.focusedElementValue(), which follows live focus) and, on `.notLanded`, retypes with `TextInjector.insert(finalText, mode: .type)` — with no re-check that the frontmost app is still the dictation target. If the user ⌘Tabs to another app within the ~1s verify window, the newly focused field is readable but doesn't contain the text → verdict `.notLanded` → the full transcript is typed character-by-character into the WRONG app (a chat box, a terminal running a command...), duplicating text that in fact landed fine in the original app. It also then persists `insertionMode = .type` for the original app (lines 2365-2369), permanently degrading its insertion mode off a false signal.
proposed_fix: Before the retype and the profile upsert, re-read `NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication?.bundleIdentifier` and require it to equal `healBundleID`; if focus moved, skip the heal entirely (no retype, no learned .type). Optionally also capture the frontmost bundle at each verifier poll and treat a focus change mid-window as `.unverifiable`.

title: Hands-free lock event is silently dropped when the latch fires before the session goes live (cold start)
description: The latch timer fires 0.5s after key-down (ActivationGesture.latchThreshold), but session arming (mic permission hop, model load, beginSession) can take multiple seconds on a cold start or after a language switch. lockDictation's `guard isDictating, sessionLive else { return }` then discards the `.lock` event permanently — it is never re-delivered. The gesture machine is in `.lockedHeld`/`.locked` (release keeps recording), so the session behaves hands-free, but the app never flips handsFreeLocked: no lock glyph, no lock earcon, and — critically — startSilenceWatchdog() never runs, so the B5 auto-stop never arms and a forgotten session records indefinitely until a manual tap.
evidence: guard isDictating, sessionLive else { return }
proposed_fix: When `.lock` arrives while isDictating but !sessionLive, stash a `pendingHandsFreeLock = true` flag instead of dropping it; in the begin task, right after `self.sessionLive = true`, check the flag and call lockDictation() (then clear the flag on every teardown path). Keep the current guard for the !isDictating case.

title: Clipboard restore races slow paste consumers: 120ms is not enough for busy Electron targets
description: pasteViaClipboard posts ⌘V and restores the previous clipboard after a fixed 120ms sleep (guarded only by changeCount equality — which still matches, because nobody else wrote). A busy target app that dequeues the synthetic ⌘V and reads NSPasteboard AFTER the restore pastes the user's PREVIOUS clipboard content instead of the dictation — the transcript is lost (it was overwritten by the restore) and arbitrary stale content lands in the field. This only occurs on the `restorePrevious: true` path (confident editable focus), which includes heavyweight native-ish apps under load; 120ms is well within observed key-event → pasteboard-read latencies for a stalled main thread.
evidence:
try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(120))
            guard myGen == restoreGeneration else { return }
proposed_fix: Increase the restore delay to ~400-500ms (still imperceptible — the paste already landed; only the restore waits), or poll: wait up to ~1s checking whether the frontmost app has processed the key event (e.g. keep the generation/changeCount guards but sleep 400ms). The changeCount guard already protects against clobbering newer writes, so a longer delay carries no correctness cost.

title: insert() reports .inserted even when the mid-flight secure-input recheck aborts the paste
description: insert() returns `.inserted` (line 87) after calling pasteViaClipboard synchronously, but inside pasteViaClipboard the recheck `guard !IsSecureEventInputEnabled() else { return }` (line 299) can silently skip posting ⌘V if secure input engaged between the entry guard and the paste (e.g. a password-manager prompt popped mid-stop). The caller then records history, sets lastInsertedDictationID (arming the B9 edit gate against text that is NOT in the field), arms the learn-from-edits watcher, and shows 'Inserted' — while the text is actually only on the clipboard and the previous clipboard snapshot is dropped without restore.
evidence: guard !IsSecureEventInputEnabled() else { return }
proposed_fix: Make pasteViaClipboard return a Bool (posted vs aborted). In insert(), when it returns false, return `.leftOnClipboard(reason: secureInputReason())` instead of `.inserted`, so the existing copy-prompt path (which already handles the secure case correctly, including the no-Scratchpad exclusion) takes over.

title: finishSessionDetailed never clears finalizedText — an unmatched finishSession returns the PREVIOUS session's transcript
description: finishSessionDetailed snapshots and clears finalizedSegments/finalizedTimedSegments/sessionWordConfidences/volatileText, but `finalizedText` is left holding the full transcript after the function returns (it is only reset by the NEXT beginSession or cancelSession). A second finishSession call without an intervening beginSession — possible on the shared engine's mixed teardown paths (MeetingRecorder calls `engine.finishSession()` on both its start-failure cleanup and stop paths; dictation error paths can leave analyzer nil while finalizedText is populated) — returns the previous transcript as if it were fresh, duplicating text into whatever consumes it.
evidence:
let result = finalizedText + joiner + volatileText
        volatileText = ""
        let segments = finalizedSegments  // finalizedText itself is never reset here
proposed_fix: In finishSessionDetailed, after computing `result`, add `finalizedText = ""` alongside the other accumulator resets, so a finish without a matching begin returns an empty transcript instead of replaying the last one.

title: DictationAssembler is dead code in the core pipeline (superseded by StreamingCleanup)
description: DictationAssembler has zero references anywhere in Sources/ or Tests/ (verified by repo-wide grep; only its own definition matches). Its role — per-segment cleanup behind speech, joined at stop — is now performed by StreamingCleanup, which endDictation actually consumes. Keeping an identically-purposed, unwired class in the audited hot path invites someone wiring the wrong one (it lacks StreamingCleanup's cancel() path used by the language-switch fallback).
evidence: final class DictationAssembler: @unchecked Sendable {  // grep: no call sites in Sources/ or Tests/
proposed_fix: Delete Sources/Talkie/DictationAssembler.swift (or, if it's being kept deliberately for a planned backend seam, add a header comment stating it is intentionally unwired and naming StreamingCleanup as the live implementation).

title: stripFillers drops sentence punctuation attached to a filler token
description: stripFillers matches fillers by trimming punctuation for the comparison (`token.trimmingCharacters(in: punctuation)`) but then drops the ENTIRE original token, punctuation included. A filler carrying sentence punctuation loses it: 'I think so, um.' → 'I think so,' (final period gone); 'Right? Um. Let's go' → 'Right? Let's go' loses the intended break. Since this net deliberately runs even after AI cleanup (as a safety net) and on the cleanup-off path, the damaged punctuation reaches the inserted text.
proposed_fix: Instead of filtering whole tokens, map each filler token to its surviving punctuation: if the trimmed token is a filler, keep the token's trailing punctuation characters (e.g. 'um.' → '.'), attach them to the previous kept token, and drop only the filler word; then run the existing spacing tidy-up.

title: Far-end watchdog give-up silently discards the multilingual merge and mislabels the meeting
description: stop() conflates 'currently capturing far end' with 'ever captured far end'. `wasFarEnd = capturingFarEnd` (line 637) is false after the zero-PCM watchdog gives up mid-meeting (tick() sets `capturingFarEnd = false` on `.gaveUp`). Consequences at stop: (1) `if let log, wasFarEnd { applyMergedSpans(spans, speaker: .them, log: log) }` drops the entire language-voted rebuild of the far stream, so all pre-give-up 'Them' turns remain the raw first-lane live output — wrong-language gibberish for non-primary spans, the exact bug the lanes exist to fix — and stay WALL-CLOCK stamped (live `log.add(.them, segment)` at line 386) while the mic side is replaced with AUDIO-CLOCK spans (line 663-666, ungated), violating TurnLog's own documented invariant ('a TurnLog must never mix the two clocks… that would corrupt cross-stream interleaving', MeetingTranscript.swift:49). (2) `participants = wasFarEnd ? ["Me", "Them"] : ["Me"]` (line 745) and `source = "talkie (mic-only)"` (line 810) claim a mic-only meeting even though the saved transcript is full of '[mm:ss] Them:' lines. (3) The single-locale `correctStreamLanguage(.them,…)` is also skipped (line 686).
proposed_fix: Track a separate `farEverActive` flag set true when the far stream starts (never reset by the watchdog downgrade). In stop(): apply `applyMergedSpans(…, .them, …)` and `correctStreamLanguage(.them,…)` whenever the far stream ran at all (gate on `farMulti != nil` / `farEngine != nil` + `farEverActive`, not the live `capturingFarEnd`); derive `participants`/`source` from `farEverActive` (or from whether the log contains .them turns) so metadata matches the transcript.

title: A late mic-tap buffer after close() re-creates the kept-audio m4a, truncating the finalized recording
description: MeetingAudioFileWriter.close() only sets `file = nil`; it never latches a 'closed' state. append() re-creates the AVAudioFile whenever `file == nil && !failed` — and `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates the existing file at that URL. The mic tap closure retains the writer directly (`return { buffer in writer.append(buffer) }`, line 492) and AudioCapture.stop() (AudioCapture.swift:344) does `removeTap` + `engine.stop()` with NO queue drain (unlike SystemAudioCapture.cleanUpCoreAudio's `ioQueue.sync {}`), so a tap callback already in flight on the render thread can enqueue an append AFTER stop() returns and after `closeAudioWriters(record: true)` (line 632) finalized the m4a. That one late buffer truncates the entire '-me.m4a' to a headerless fragment while `keepAudioFiles["Me"]` still records it as playable (close() already returned true). The cancelled-start paths have the sibling bug: closeAudioWriters(record:false) deletes the file (line 516-518), then a late append resurrects an orphan file that nothing ever cleans up.
proposed_fix: Add a `private var closed = false` to MeetingAudioFileWriter, set it inside close()'s `queue.sync` block, and change append()'s guard to `guard !failed, !closed else { return }`. This makes close() a true latch regardless of capture-thread drain timing (and fixes both the truncation and the deleted-file resurrection).

title: Multilingual mic lanes leak when audio.start() throws — analyzers left running, later sessions degraded
description: In start()'s multilingual mic branch, `mm.start(...)` succeeds (2-4 live SpeechAnalyzers spun up) and then `try audio.start(...)` can throw (e.g. `TalkieEngineError.noInputDevice` when only an output-only Bluetooth device is present). Control jumps to the catch at line 354, which cancels `micMulti` — but `micMulti = mm` (line 330) was never reached, so `mm.cancel()` is never called: the lanes' analyzers, reader tasks, and fanout stream are abandoned live. Compounding it, AudioCapture.start() stores `self.continuation = continuation` BEFORE `try installAndStart()` and does not clear it on throw (AudioCapture.swift:141-155), so the lanes' input stream is retained even after the failure. The far-end branch handles this correctly (`else { await fm.cancel() }` after a `try?`); only the mic branch throws through. Leaked analyzers can then make the user's retry hit the system concurrent-analyzer cap, silently degrading the next meeting to single-locale.
proposed_fix: Wrap the mic `audio.start` in its own do/catch that runs `await mm.cancel()` before rethrowing (or assign `micMulti = mm` before `try audio.start` so the existing catch cleans it up, then nil it there on failure). Additionally, mirror SystemAudioCapture in AudioCapture.start(): clear the retained session parameters (`continuation`, `captured`, callbacks) when `installAndStart()` throws.

title: A queued tick surviving timer invalidation can start an analyzer rotation that overlaps stop()'s finish
description: tick() has no `isRecording`/`isFinishing` guard (only `guard let startedAt`, line 537). The timer closure spawns `Task { @MainActor in self?.tick() }` (line 462), so a tick enqueued just before stop() runs `timer?.invalidate()` survives invalidation and executes at stop()'s first suspension point (e.g. `await rotationTask?.value` or `await mic.finish(...)`). At that moment `startedAt`, `micMulti`/`farMulti` are all still set, so if `elapsed - lastRotationElapsed >= 600` (stop lands within ~1s of a rotation boundary) the stale tick assigns a NEW rotationTask and calls `rotate()` — concurrent with the `finish()` stop() is about to run (or already running) on the same MultiLangStreamTranscriber actor. That is precisely the overlap the code documents as forbidden ('rotation and finish both mutate lane state … and must not overlap', line 653): actor reentrancy lets rotate() swap in fresh generations and append to `lane.collected` while finish() is mid-harvest, dropping the retired generation's words from the final transcript (finish reads `lane.collected` before rotate appends) or finalizing a generation twice. The stale tick can also spuriously re-run checkHealth and flush the crash partial mid-stop (harmless today, but only by accident of ordering).
proposed_fix: Add `guard isRecording, !isFinishing else { return }` at the top of tick() (MeetingRecorder is @MainActor, and stop() flips `isRecording = false` synchronously before its first await, so any stale tick then no-ops). Alternatively/additionally, have stop() await `rotationTask` AFTER re-reading it in a loop until nil, but the tick guard is simpler and sufficient.

title: 'Regenerate summary' permanently destroys the user's typed meeting notes
description: The user's live notes typed during a recording survive ONLY inside `Meeting.summary` (either as the fused body or under '## Your notes' — MeetingRecorder.composeSummary; `recorder.notes` is cleared after save and the raw notes are persisted nowhere else). regenerateSummary() replaces the whole summary with a fresh transcript-only summary (`updated.summary = summary; store.update(updated)`), which also rewrites the .md on disk. One click of the hover refresh button on any meeting that had notes irreversibly deletes those notes with no confirmation and no undo.
evidence:
guard let summary = await MeetingSummarizer().summarize(meeting.transcript) else { return }
var updated = meeting
updated.summary = summary
store.update(updated)
proposed_fix: Preserve user notes across regeneration: extract a '## Your notes' section (or the fused body) from the existing summary and re-compose via MeetingRecorder.composeSummary(userNotes:transcriptSummary:fused:) with the fresh transcript summary; at minimum, gate the button with a confirmation when the current summary contains '## Your notes' or was fusion-produced. Longer-term, persist raw notes as their own Meeting field so no summary rewrite can lose them.

title: MeetingStore.delete's path-escape guard misses ".." — FileShredder would recursively delete outside the meetings folder
description: The delete-time guard for `audioFiles` values only rejects empty strings and names containing "/". The value ".." passes, and `meetingsDirectoryURL.appendingPathComponent("..")` resolves to the PARENT of ~/Talkie Meetings (the home directory). FileShredder.shred() explicitly skips the overwrite for non-regular files and falls through to `FileManager.removeItem(at:)` (FileShredder.swift: 'anything else (directory, symlink, missing) skips straight to removeItem'), which removes directories recursively. The values are normally app-generated, but the guard's stated purpose is exactly to stop a non-plain-filename from a tampered/corrupt meetings.json from escaping the folder — and it fails to. A symlink basename inside the folder would similarly redirect the shred outside it.
proposed_fix: Tighten the filter to a strict single-component check, e.g. `where !name.isEmpty && name != "." && name != ".." && (name as NSString).lastPathComponent == name && !name.hasPrefix(".")`, and/or verify `url.standardizedFileURL.path.hasPrefix(meetingsDirectoryURL.standardizedFileURL.path + "/")` before shredding. Consider making FileShredder refuse directories outright (remove only regular files).

title: InboxWatcher silently moves a never-transcribed file to Transcribed/ when its filename matches any past import
description: The reconcile step treats 'a meeting whose `source` contains `(imported: <filename>)`' as proof THIS file was imported, but the marker is filename-only. Voice Memos AirDropped from iOS reuse default names ('New Recording.m4a'); the second, different recording dropped into the watched folder matches the first import's marker on the very first scan and is moved straight into Transcribed/ — never transcribed, with no error, no skip entry, no banner (unlike the coordinator's dupe guard, which at least reports 'skipped: already imported'). The user's stated mental model ('files that land here are transcribed…then moved') is silently violated and the recording looks processed when it is not.
proposed_fix: Strengthen the done-marker beyond the bare filename: include file size and/or content-modification date in the stored `source` fragment (e.g. `(imported: name|bytes|mtime)`) and match on that; or before moving an un-enqueued candidate, compare its size against the matched meeting's kept audio copy and re-import on mismatch. At minimum, surface a user-visible notice when a file is moved without being transcribed in this session.

title: StreamLanguageVoter.mergeWords is O(frames × words) — multi-hour multilingual meetings stall the stop pipeline
description: Step 1 scans EVERY valid word for EVERY 0.12s frame (`for w in valid where w.start <= mid && w.end >= mid`). A 2-hour bilingual meeting is ~60,000 frames × (2-4 lanes × ~15-20k words) ≈ several billion comparisons, run once per stream inside stop()'s finalize — the UI sits in 'Transcribing & summarizing…' for the duration. The word-keep step (line 94-102) re-scans each word's frame range, which is fine, but the raw-winner pass dominates.
proposed_fix: Bucket words by frame index once (O(W × framesPerWord)): for each word, add its (confidence, locale) to every frame it covers via `frameIndex(start)...frameIndex(end)`, keeping the max-confidence locale per frame. This makes the vote linear in total word-frames and removes the O(F×W) product.

title: 'Start recording' button uses && instead of || — enabled-but-dead when speech recognition is unavailable
description: The button is disabled only when BOTH the summarizer (FoundationModels) and the transcription engine (Speech) are unavailable. When Apple Intelligence is available but on-device speech is not, the button stays enabled, and `recorder.start()` silently returns false at `guard … TranscriptionEngine.isAvailable else { return false }` (MeetingRecorder.swift:238) — the user clicks Start and nothing happens, with no feedback. Transcription availability is the hard requirement; summarization is optional.

proposed_fix: Change to `.disabled(!TranscriptionEngine.isAvailable)` (summaries degrade gracefully to an empty string, so summarizer availability shouldn't gate recording), and optionally show an explanatory subtitle when disabled.

title: Mic-capture-failure callback is dropped during the start() window — meeting can go live recording silence
description: handleMicCaptureFailure guards on `isRecording, !isFinishing`. The mic capture (and its AVAudioEngineConfigurationChange observer) goes live early in start(), but `isRecording` only becomes true at the commit block — after the calendar lookup and the whole far-end setup, which contain multiple awaits. A device change that kills the mic in that window (AirPods disconnect at meeting start is a classic) fires onCaptureFailed, the handler no-ops, and start() then commits: the meeting runs with the pill/timer showing healthy while the mic captures nothing. The far-end watchdog is also neutered: `audio.secondsSinceLastBuffer()` returns nil → micAlive=false → the watchdog holds .ok forever.
evidence:
guard isRecording, !isFinishing else { return }
Task { await stop() }
proposed_fix: In handleMicCaptureFailure, also handle the starting state: `if isStarting { cancelStart = true; return }` so an in-flight start aborts and returns false instead of committing with a dead mic.

title: Watchdog tap rebuild discards the rolling far-end audio buffer used for stop-time language correction
description: buildAndStart() unconditionally replaces `captured` with a fresh CapturedAudio (`captured = capture`). It is shared by start() AND the watchdog's rebuild(), so every mid-meeting tap rebuild throws away up to 10 minutes of buffered far-end PCM. In the multilingual-fallback configuration (bufferAudio=true: user speaks >1 language but the lanes couldn't start), stop()'s `correctStreamLanguage(.them, … buffers: systemAudio.bufferedAudio() …)` then sees only post-rebuild audio, so the language self-consistency check and any re-transcription run on a truncated window — weakening exactly the correction the buffer exists for.
evidence:
let capture = bufferAudio
    ? CapturedAudio(maxFrames: …)
    : nil
captured = capture
proposed_fix: Create the CapturedAudio ring only in start() (where the session begins) and keep the existing instance across rebuild() — e.g. `if captured == nil { captured = bufferAudio ? CapturedAudio(…) : nil }` in buildAndStart, or move the creation out of buildAndStart into start(). The ring is already drop-oldest, so appending across a rebuild is safe.

title: A corrupt/unreadable JSON file silently loads as empty and is permanently overwritten on the next save (7+ stores)
description: HistoryStore.load() is `guard let data = try? Data(contentsOf:), let decoded = try? JSONDecoder().decode(...) else { return }` — any read or decode failure leaves the store empty, and the very next mutation's save() atomically overwrites the file, destroying the old bytes with no backup. The same wipe-on-next-save pattern exists in ContextGraphStore.load (ContextGraph/ContextGraphStore.swift:160 — worse: the backfill watermark file usually still decodes, so backfill also refuses to re-seed the emptied graph), StatsStore.load (StatsStore.swift:241 — lifetime totals), ActivityStore.load (ActivityStore.swift:252 — months of streak/heatmap history, irreplaceable), WordFrequencyStore.load (WordFrequencyStore.swift:224), ScratchpadStore.load (Scratchpad/ScratchpadStore.swift:155 — includes user-typed notes that even "Clear everything" promises to keep), AppUsageStore.load (AppUsageStore.swift:143), and ContextSummary.load. DictionaryStore.load (DictionaryStore.swift:54-107) already solves exactly this with a quarantine-move to `.corrupt` and an explicit no-save-on-failure rule — the other stores never got the pattern.

Factor the load-with-quarantine into one shared helper and adopt it in HistoryStore, ContextGraphStore (both entities.json and the watermark: also reset the .dictation/.meeting watermark when entities.json is quarantined so backfill can re-seed from retained history/meetings), StatsStore, ActivityStore, WordFrequencyStore, ScratchpadStore, AppUsageStore, and AutoAddPreviewLog.

title: HistoryStore.flush() has zero callers and there is no applicationWillTerminate — the debounced history write is lost on quit
description: HistoryStore.save() only schedules a 250 ms-debounced write on HistoryFileWriter; flush() exists "(app teardown / tests)" but `grep -rn "flush()" Sources` shows no app call site, and `grep applicationWillTerminate Sources` returns nothing (main.swift and AppDelegate install no termination hook). Every other store writes synchronously, so quitting within the debounce window desynchronizes history.json from its derived stores: (a) the last dictation is in stats/graph/wordFreq but missing from history; (b) worse, deleting a dictation in MemoryView persists all the purges immediately but the history deletion itself is debounced — quit within 250 ms and the "deleted" transcript resurrects in history.json on next launch while its graph/wordFreq/scratchpad traces stay purged (and backfill won't re-ingest it because the watermark already covers its timestamp).

proposed_fix: Implement `applicationWillTerminate(_:)` in AppDelegate and run `await history.flush()` (bridging with a short semaphore/RunLoop wait, or make the delete/clearAll paths write through immediately instead of debounced — deletions are rare and small, so calling flush() right after delete() is the simplest correct fix).

title: Deleting a meeting leaves the persisted Brief (context_summary.json) quoting the meeting's extracted commitments
description: MeetingsView.deleteMeeting runs `store.delete(meeting)` + `contextGraph?.purge(source: .meeting, ...)` and stops. But the Brief is generated from graph commitments and people/projects — which include meeting-sourced entities (ContextSummary.swift:29-37) — and is persisted verbatim in context_summary.json. The dictation-delete path clears it for exactly this reason (MemoryView.swift:123 `contextSummary?.clearSummary()` — "Cleared on every delete so context_summary.json can't keep quoting text you just deleted"), and the meeting-delete confirmation dialog promises "Deletes the transcript and everything Talkie's memory extracted from this meeting", yet the stale Brief keeps quoting the purged commitments until the next refresh happens to overwrite it.

contextGraph?.purge(source: .meeting, sourceID: meeting.id.uuidString)
pendingDelete = nil   // no contextSummary clear
proposed_fix: Inject ContextSummaryStore into MeetingsView (same optional-with-nil-default pattern as MemoryView) and add `contextSummary?.clearSummary()` to deleteMeeting, wiring it at the SettingsView construction site.

title: Voice-edit updateText breaks WordFrequencyStore's record/purge inverse — later delete corrupts other dictations' counts
description: WordFrequencyStore's contract is "Recording a text then purging the same text returns the store to where it started" (WordFrequencyStore.swift:54-57), and MemoryView.deleteDictation purges by the entry's CURRENT text (`wordFreq.purge(text: entry.text)`, MemoryView.swift:118). But a B9 voice edit rewrites the entry in place via HistoryStore.updateText (`entries[idx].text = trimmed`) without touching wordFreq (the doc note only considered stats/graph double-counting). Delete that entry later and purge tokenizes the EDITED text: the original tokens stay inflated forever, and the edited-in tokens — never recorded for this entry — get decremented anyway, silently stealing counts from OTHER dictations that legitimately used those words (floor-at-0 hides the damage).
evidence: entries[idx].text = trimmed   // wordFreq recorded the ORIGINAL finalText at ingest; purge later uses entry.text
proposed_fix: In AppDelegate.runVoiceEdit's ReplaceWordIntent branch (and its Undo closure), keep the frequency store in step with the in-place rewrite: `wordFreq.purge(text: original); wordFreq.record(text: edited)` next to the `history.updateText` calls (and the inverse on Undo). This preserves updateText's deliberate no-re-ingestion of stats/graph while restoring the wordFreq inverse invariant.

title: Cancelled search rebuild still writes the vector sidecar — a stale save can overwrite a newer one (including right after 'Clear everything')
description: scheduleRebuild cancels the prior outer Task, but the embedding work runs in `Task.detached`, which does not inherit cancellation — an already-started older rebuild continues and unconditionally runs `sidecar.save(vectorsByHash: index.vectorsByHash)`. The `guard !Task.isCancelled` only protects `apply()`. Two overlapping rebuilds' saves are unordered (the older corpus is usually the slower embed), so the on-disk sidecar can end up reflecting the OLDER snapshot — e.g. re-writing hashes/vectors of dictations the user just deleted, or landing after MemoryView.clearEverything's `searchEngine.clearSidecar()` and repopulating the cache that was just wiped (hashes+floats only, no text, and it self-heals on the next rebuild — hence low).
proposed_fix: Move the `sidecar.save` out of the detached closure: return the built index, and only after the outer task's `guard !Task.isCancelled` passes (i.e. this is still the newest rebuild) perform the save (it can hop to a utility task, but gated on the cancellation check). Alternatively pass a monotonic generation into the closure and have the sidecar drop stale generations, mirroring HistoryFileWriter.

title: ContextGraphStore re-encodes the entire graph synchronously on the main actor on every dictation completion
description: ContextGraphStore.save() JSON-encodes up to 2,000 entities × 12 provenance entries (each with a 120-char snippet — potentially megabyte-scale JSON) plus the watermark, and writes both files, all on @MainActor. It runs on the dictation hot path (AppDelegate:2198 `contextGraph.ingest` → save()) and again per backfill. HistoryStore was explicitly rearchitected onto an off-main writer actor because "the dictation-completion path never blocks the UI on JSON + disk I/O" (HistoryStore.swift:30-35), but the graph — the largest file in the layer — still does exactly that, as do WordFrequencyStore/StatsStore/ScratchpadStore saves on the same completion path (those are small; the graph is the one that scales).
proposed_fix: Reuse the HistoryFileWriter pattern: snapshot `Array(entities.values)` (Entity is Sendable) plus the watermark, and hand encode+write to a generation-guarded writer actor with a short debounce, keeping cap-enforcement on the main actor before snapshotting. Add a flush() and call it from the same applicationWillTerminate hook as HistoryStore's.

title: clearAll's shred-race comment is wrong: an in-flight writer-actor write is not stopped by pendingSave.cancel()
description: clearAll() claims "Cancel any in-flight debounced write first so it can't race the shred and re-materialize the old bytes between the overwrite and the empty rewrite." But cancel() only helps while the debounce Task is still sleeping; a task that already passed its `guard !Task.isCancelled` and is awaiting `writer.write(snapshot, generation:)` proceeds regardless, and its atomic write re-creates history.json with the FULL pre-clear transcript bytes AFTER FileShredder.shred ran (the actor then serializes the empty write after it, so the final visible state is correct — but the un-shredded old bytes now sit in a fresh inode, exactly what the shred tried to prevent). Low because FileShredder's own header already concedes APFS/atomic-write limits, but the code comment asserts a guarantee the code doesn't provide.
evidence:
pendingSave?.cancel()
pendingSave = nil
FileShredder.shred(fileURL)   // an already-dequeued writer.write(oldSnapshot) can still land after this
proposed_fix: Serialize the shred through the writer actor so it orders after any in-flight write: add `func shredAndClear()` on HistoryFileWriter that bumps latestWritten past all pending generations, shreds, then writes the empty array; have clearAll() call it (fire-and-forget Task is fine — the actor guarantees ordering). At minimum, correct the comment to say the race is only narrowed, not closed.

title: DictionaryStore quarantines the user's dictionary on a transient READ failure, not just on decode failure
description: load()'s failure guard collapses two very different cases: `try? Data(contentsOf:)` failing (transient I/O — the on-disk JSON may be perfectly valid) and JSONDecoder failing (genuine corruption). Both paths call quarantineCorruptFile(), which moves the user's curated dictionary.json aside to `.corrupt` (deleting any previous `.corrupt` first) and falls back to defaults — so one transient read error silently sidelines the whole curated vocab, and the next UI-driven save() writes the default single-rule dictionary over the canonical path. The user only recovers by manually finding the .corrupt file.
proposed_fix: Split the guard: if `Data(contentsOf:)` throws while the file exists, do NOT quarantine — keep in-memory defaults for the session and set a `loadFailed` flag that save() checks (refuse to write until a subsequent successful load), so a transient read error can neither move nor overwrite the good file. Quarantine only when bytes were read but failed to decode.

title: Pinned meeting-transcription language survives removal from spoken languages: blank Picker + silent wrong-language pinning
description: The Meetings tab's "Transcription language" Picker offers only "auto" plus the CURRENT settings.spokenLanguages. AppSettings.meetingLanguageMode is never sanitized when a language is removed (AppSettings.swift:228-229 only persists it; spokenLanguages.didSet at AppSettings.swift:218-225 doesn't touch it). If the user pins e.g. "de-DE" and later removes German from Languages, the Picker selection matches no tag (SwiftUI renders it blank and logs an invalid-selection warning), and MeetingRecorder.start() keeps pinning both streams to the removed locale: `let pinned = (mode != "auto" && !mode.isEmpty) ? mode : nil ... micLocale = pinned` (MeetingRecorder.swift:268-277), which also disables the multilingual detect path (`multiLang = (pinned == nil) && langs.count > 1`).

proposed_fix: Sanitize in AppSettings: in spokenLanguages.didSet (AppSettings.swift:~218), add `if meetingLanguageMode != "auto" && !spokenLanguages.contains(meetingLanguageMode) { meetingLanguageMode = "auto" }`. Optionally also guard at load (AppSettings.swift:524) so a stale persisted value resets to "auto".

title: "Start recording" silently no-ops when MeetingRecorder.start() refuses (mic denied, dictation in flight, speech unavailable)
description: The record button discards start()'s Bool: `Button("Start recording") { Task { await recorder.start() } }`. start() returns false with no UI side effect when mic access is denied, a dictation/polish is in flight, or TranscriptionEngine is unavailable (MeetingRecorder.swift:237-247). The user taps and nothing visibly happens. The App-Intent path deliberately throws on false (`AppDelegate.toggleMeetingRecordingFromIntent`, AppDelegate.swift:3231-3239) but the UI path has no equivalent. Also the disabled() gate mismatches start()'s guard: the button is disabled only when BOTH summarizer AND transcription are unavailable (line 228), while start() requires TranscriptionEngine alone — so with speech unavailable but Apple Intelligence on, the button is enabled yet start() always returns false.

proposed_fix: Capture the result: `Task { if await recorder.start() == false { startFailed = true } }` with a new @State driving a SettingsNote/alert naming the likely cause (mic permission, dictation in progress, speech unavailable). Change the disabled condition to `!TranscriptionEngine.isAvailable` to match start()'s actual guard.

title: Main window position is reset every launch: window.center() runs after setFrameAutosaveName restores the saved frame
description: MainWindowController.init sets the autosave name (which immediately restores any saved frame from defaults) and then unconditionally calls window.center(), clobbering the restored position. The user's window position is therefore never remembered across launches — the frame is saved on move (autosave name is set) but discarded at startup; only the saved size survives.

window.setFrameAutosaveName("TalkieMainWindow")
        window.center()
proposed_fix:
Only center when no frame was saved: replace the two lines with `if !window.setFrameUsingName("TalkieMainWindow") { window.center() }
window.setFrameAutosaveName("TalkieMainWindow")` (setFrameUsingName returns false when defaults hold no frame).

title: Hand-edited transcript is invisible for meetings with kept audio — playback view keeps rendering stale segment text
description: saveTranscript (line 492) writes only `updated.transcript = edited`; meeting.segments are untouched. But when the meeting kept audio, the expanded row branch prefers MeetingPlaybackView, which renders `segment.text` per row — the pre-edit text. So after Save, the user's fix vanishes from the visible transcript (it only lands in the .md, Copy, and the next edit session). For audio-less meetings the plain `Text(meeting.transcript)` branch shows the edit, so behavior is inconsistent between the two kinds of meetings. The code comments only scope out re-aligning TIMINGS, not displaying the edited text.

title: Per-app "Insert in" picker shows a duplicate "As spoken" row (synthetic placeholder is iterated into the menu)
description: outputLanguageOptions deliberately puts a synthetic `LanguageOption(code: "", name: "As spoken")` at index 0 purely for the `count > 1` gate (line 455-457), but the Picker's ForEach iterates ALL options, so the menu renders: "As spoken" (tag nil), "Adaptive (auto-detect)", then a second "As spoken" (tag Optional("")), then the real languages. The duplicate row can never show as selected (the binding getter maps empty code to nil, which matches the first row), so users see a confusing dead duplicate entry in every profile editor that offers output languages.

proposed_fix: Iterate only real languages: `ForEach(outputLanguageOptions.dropFirst(), id: \.code)` — or filter `outputLanguageOptions.filter { !$0.code.isEmpty }` — leaving the synthetic element solely for the count gate.

title: Import-preview sheet identity churns: PreviewBox mints a fresh UUID on every binding read, so any re-render re-presents the sheet
description: The Dictionary import sheet uses `.sheet(item:)` with a computed Binding whose getter constructs `PreviewBox(preview:)` anew — and PreviewBox declares `let id = UUID()`, so the item's identity changes on every body evaluation. While the preview sheet is open, any change to an observed store (DictionarySettings observes `dictionary` and `nicheVocab`; both can mutate from background learning, the dictation pipeline, or MCP teach-back confirms while the user reviews) re-evaluates the binding, and SwiftUI treats the new UUID as a different item — dismissing and re-presenting the sheet (flicker/animation restart) mid-review.
evidence: private struct PreviewBox: Identifiable { let id = UUID(); let preview: MergePreview } ... .sheet(item: Binding(get: { pendingPreview.map { PreviewBox(preview: $0) } }, ...
proposed_fix: Give the staged preview a stable identity: stage `@State private var pendingBox: PreviewBox?` once in openPack/installStarterPack/importFromCompetitor (creating the UUID a single time) and use `.sheet(item: $pendingBox)` directly, clearing pendingPack alongside it in onDismiss.

title: Memory search runs the full semantic scan synchronously inside body on every keystroke
description: `searchResults` calls `searchEngine.search(trimmedQuery)` directly in the view body with no debounce and no caching. SemanticIndex.search embeds the query via NLEmbedding and cosine-scores EVERY chunk of every record on the main thread (SemanticIndex.swift:267-297). With a 2,000-entry history plus chunked meeting transcripts this runs per keystroke — and again on every unrelated re-render of MemoryView (it observes six stores) — producing typing jank in the search field on large libraries.
evidence: @ViewBuilder private var searchResults: some View { let hits = searchEngine.search(trimmedQuery) ...
proposed_fix: Hold `@State private var hits: [SearchHit] = []` and populate via `.task(id: trimmedQuery)` with a ~150ms debounce, running the scoring off the main actor (mirror SearchEngine's existing storesChanged rebuild pattern: snapshot the index, `await Task.detached { index.search(q) }.value`).

title: MCP setup prompt omits the retitle_meeting tool (17 of 18 tools) and the drift gate doesn't cover it

title: Microphone "Input device" Picker goes blank when the pinned device is absent, and the device list never refreshes
description: The Picker binds $settings.preferredInputDeviceUID (String?) against tags built from `devices`, which is loaded exactly once in `.onAppear { devices = AudioDevices.inputDevices() }` (line 1475). If the pinned mic is unplugged (or the user plugs one in while the pane is open), the stored UID matches no tag: SwiftUI renders an empty selection and logs an invalid-selection warning, and there is no visible indication that Talkie is still pinned to a missing device (the capture layer falls back silently).

title: Dictionary pane persists the whole dictionary to disk on every keystroke
description: ReplacementRow's TextFields bind directly into `$dictionary.replacements`, so every typed character mutates the published array; `.onChange(of: dictionary.replacements) { _, _ in dictionary.save() }` then JSON-encodes and atomically rewrites dictionary.json per keystroke (DictionaryStore.save() at DictionaryStore.swift:109-115). Same for `.onChange(of: dictionary.vocabulary)`. Correct but wasteful, and each change also fans out through everything observing DictionaryStore.
evidence:
.onChange(of: dictionary.replacements) { _, _ in dictionary.save() }
        .onChange(of: dictionary.vocabulary) { _, _ in dictionary.save() }
proposed_fix: Debounce the save: keep the onChange but route through a small `@State saveTask: Task<Void,Never>?` that cancels and re-schedules `try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(400)); dictionary.save()` — plus an unconditional save in onDisappear so a quick tab switch can't lose the last keystrokes.

title: DashboardView observes a SettingsRouter it never uses

title: "Note this" voice notes are written without .md extension and silently overwrite each other within the same minute
description: TalkieFolderDestination.write uses note.suggestedFileName verbatim: `AppPaths.meetingsDirectory().appendingPathComponent(note.suggestedFileName)`. Meeting notes are safe (Meeting.fileName is "yyyy-MM-dd-HHmm-<uuid4>-meeting.md"), but dictation notes from the "note this …" voice command (AppDelegate.swift:1912 → NoteComposers.dictationNote) set suggestedFileName via `NoteTemplate.fileName("{datetime}-note", for: note, existing: [])` (NoteComposers.swift:140) — which returns a base WITHOUT an extension and with an EMPTY collision set (the comment claims "the destination de-collides the rest", but TalkieFolderDestination performs no de-collision, unlike ObsidianVaultDestination). With the default export destination (.talkieFolder), a note is written as e.g. "2026-07-09-1432-note" (no .md, so Finder/Obsidian/Markdown tooling won't treat it as Markdown), and a second "note this" in the same minute writes the identical filename with .atomic — silently destroying the first note while the HUD reports "Saved". The datetime template has minute granularity, so two notes per minute is a completely normal usage pattern.

proposed_fix: In TalkieFolderDestination.write, mirror ObsidianVaultDestination: (1) if note.suggestedFileName has no path extension, list the target directory's existing base names, run the base through NoteTemplate.deCollide (or reuse NoteTemplate.fileName with the real `existing` set), and append ".md"; (2) keep meeting filenames (which already end in .md and embed a uuid) untouched by only applying the de-collide/extension logic when `!note.suggestedFileName.hasSuffix(".md")`. Alternatively change NoteComposers.dictationNote to emit "{datetime}-note.md" AND make TalkieFolderDestination de-collide against FileManager.contentsOfDirectory before writing.

title: Updater swap script deletes the running app bundle even when the old process never exited (30s timeout falls through to rm -rf)
description: spawnSwap's shell script waits for the old Talkie PID with `while kill -0 "$PID"…` but the loop guard is `[ "$i" -gt 150 ] && break` — after ~30s it BREAKS and proceeds to `rm -rf "$DEST"` + swap + `open` regardless of whether the process exited. installAndRelaunch calls `NSApp.terminate(nil)` after spawning the script; if termination stalls (main thread wedged on one of the app's known synchronous AX hangs, a modal alert/runModal session at the wrong moment, or any future applicationShouldTerminate delay), the script deletes /Applications/Talkie.app out from under the still-running instance, swaps in the new bundle, and launches a second instance while the first is alive — running-from-deleted-bundle breakage, two instances racing on history.json/settings, and the single-instance handoff in main.swift then makes the freshly-opened copy exit(0) and merely activate the zombie old instance, so the update appears to have installed but the OLD build keeps running.
evidence:
i=$((i + 1))
  [ "$i" -gt 150 ] && break
done
rm -rf "$DEST.tmp-update"
proposed_fix: Make the timeout abort instead of fall through: replace `[ "$i" -gt 150 ] && break` with `[ "$i" -gt 150 ] && exit 1` (optionally logging to a file in the Updates dir so the settings card can surface "update staged but the app didn't exit — relaunch to retry"). The staged app remains in staging for a retry; nothing is lost by aborting.

title: AXFieldReader's descendant search is a combinatorially unbounded synchronous AX walk on the main thread with no messaging timeout
description: findTextDescendant recurses to depth 8 with up to 40 children per node — a worst-case budget of 40^8 nodes with NO total node cap (only logFocusedTree has a lines.count>80 cap). Each node costs up to 3 synchronous AX IPC round-trips (roleOf, stringValue, children), each of which can block up to the default 6-second AX messaging timeout on a busy/cold-launching target (no AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout call exists anywhere in Sources/). The walk triggers precisely in Electron/Chromium apps (Claude, Slack, VS Code) whose focused element has an empty value — the apps with the largest AX trees (tens of thousands of nodes within depth 8) — and focusedElementValue can run the DFS up to three times (focused element, app focused element, focused window). Callers are all @MainActor: InsertionVerifier.verify polls it 4× per insertion (InsertionVerifier.swift:64) and LearningEngine's edit watcher polls it repeatedly (LearningEngine.swift:48). This is the same "synchronous, no-timeout AX reads of whatever's frontmost can hang indefinitely" failure class the MusicController header documents as the cause of the stuck-isProcessing bug — the trigger was removed but the unbounded walk remains. Fix does NOT involve gating injection on focus detection (deliberately off-limits); it only bounds diagnostic/verification reads.
evidence: if depth > 8 { return nil } … for child in children(el).prefix(40) { if let hit = findTextDescendant(child, depth: depth + 1) { return hit } }
proposed_fix: (1) Add a total visited-node budget to findTextDescendant (e.g. an inout counter capped at ~500 nodes) so the DFS is linear-bounded, not depth×breadth-bounded. (2) On each AXUIElement obtained in AXFieldReader (and ContextCapture), call AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout(el, 0.5) so one unresponsive app can't block a read for 6s per call. Both changes preserve behavior on responsive apps (the reader is documented best-effort and callers already handle nil).
verifier_notes:

Verified point by point:

1. Unbounded walk, no node cap — Sources/Talkie/AXFieldReader.swift:59-65: `if depth > 8 { return nil }` ... `for child in children(el).prefix(40)`. There is no total node counter or time budget in findTextDescendant; the only node cap in the file is in the diagnostic logFocusedTree (line 107: `if depth > 6 || lines.count > 80 { return }`), exactly as the finder said. 4. Trigger condition — stringValue guards `!s.isEmpty` (line 80), so an EMPTY focused field (the normal state when starting dictation into Claude/Slack/VS Code, whose focused element is a generic group) falls through to the DFS at line 32. focusedElementValue can run the DFS up to 3 times (line 32, plus the 2-attribute fallback loop at lines 36-40). Known-deliberate check: no conflict. The finding explicitly does not propose gating injection on focus detection (rule 1); bounding verification/diagnostic reads (total node cap, AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout, or hoisting off the main thread) leaves the injection path untouched.

Severity rationale (high, not critical): it is a real, previously-observed-in-production main-thread hang class, retriggerable per-poll for up to ~60s after every insertion via LearningEngine and on the hot dictation path via AppDelegate:2097; but the worst case needs a busy/unresponsive frontmost app, the common responsive-Electron case degrades to multi-second UI jank rather than an indefinite hang, and there is no data-loss/security dimension. | [real/high] Verified in code. title: Permissions 'Relaunch now' races the app's exit (fixed 0.4s sleep) and breaks on paths with shell metacharacters
description: relaunch() runs `sh -c "sleep 0.4; open \"<bundlePath>\""` then NSApp.terminate(nil). Two defects: (a) if the app takes longer than 0.4s to exit, `open` targets the still-running instance — LaunchServices just activates the dying process instead of launching a fresh one, then the app exits and never comes back. This is the exact race UpdateInstaller.spawnSwap solves with a kill-0 poll loop, and it hits the one flow where a fresh process is mandatory (the Input-Monitoring TCC quirk where the event tap can't install without relaunch): the user taps "Relaunch now", Talkie quits, nothing reopens, and the hotkey remains dead. (b) the bundle path is interpolated inside a double-quoted shell string with no escaping — a path containing `"`, `$`, or backtick (e.g. a user folder named with quotes) breaks the command or executes as shell; compare shQuote in UpdateInstaller.swift:155 which handles this correctly.
evidence: task.arguments = ["-c", "sleep 0.4; open \"\(path)\""]
proposed_fix: Reuse the UpdateInstaller pattern: generate the command as `PID=<pid>; while kill -0 $PID 2>/dev/null; do sleep 0.2; done; open '<single-quoted path>'` with the path escaped via the same shQuote helper ('\'' escaping), or factor shQuote into a shared spot. This removes both the fixed-sleep race and the quoting hole.

title: Privacy doctor report reads the context-graph store from the wrong path — always reports it as 'not created yet'
description: dataSection decodes graph entities from `paths.support.appendingPathComponent("entities.json")`, but the store actually lives at `<support>/graph/entities.json` (ContextGraphStore.swift:38-45 creates the "graph" subdirectory; TalkieMCP/TalkieStore.swift:285 reads "graph/entities.json"). The 'Your data' section of the privacy receipt — whose whole point is showing the user every place their data lives — therefore always prints `entities.json — not created yet` and omits the size/count of the file that holds the most personal content (entity names plus literal provenance snippets of dictated speech). The same section also lists `niche/vocab.json` correctly, so this is a one-line path drift, not a pattern.

proposed_fix: Change the three occurrences at DoctorReport.swift:254-257 to `paths.support.appendingPathComponent("graph/entities.json")` (keep the displayed name as `graph/entities.json` so the receipt shows the true location). Also add `graph/backfill-watermark.json` to the existence-only list if completeness is desired.

title: Updater Shell.run can deadlock on large stderr output (sequential pipe drain), hanging the update check/download forever
description: Shell.run reads stdout to EOF, THEN stderr to EOF, then waits: `let outData = outPipe…readDataToEndOfFile(); let errData = errPipe…readDataToEndOfFile(); p.waitUntilExit()`. If the child writes more than the ~64KB pipe buffer to stderr while its stdout is still open (e.g. `gh` emitting a long error trace, verbose auth diagnostics, or download progress when it mis-detects a TTY), the child blocks writing stderr while Shell.run blocks reading stdout — a classic mutual deadlock. The comment ("Drain before waiting so a large payload can't deadlock on a full pipe") only covers the large-STDOUT case. Because every gh/ditto/xattr call in the updater funnels through this (ghListReleases, ghDownload, GH.isAuthenticated, unzip, de-quarantine), a deadlock leaves AppUpdater stuck in .checking/.downloading/.installing with isBusy==true for the rest of the app run — the settings card can never retry.
evidence: let outData = outPipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()\nlet errData = errPipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile()\np.waitUntilExit()
proposed_fix: Drain the two pipes concurrently: read stderr on a background thread/DispatchQueue (or set readabilityHandler on both file handles accumulating into locked buffers), then waitUntilExit and join. E.g. `let errThread = Thread { errData = errPipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile() }; errThread.start();` before reading stdout, then join before returning.

title: talkie CLI --locale silently falls back to en-US for unsupported locales while claiming to prepare the requested model
description: FileTranscriber.locale() resolves the requested locale via SpeechTranscriber.supportedLocale; when the requested locale isn't supported it silently substitutes en-US and only throws if even en-US is unavailable. The CLI (Sources/TalkieCLI/main.swift:134 and DictateCommand.swift:255) prints "Preparing on-device model for <requested locale>…" and then transcribes with the English model — so `talkie transcribe interview.m4a --locale sw-KE` (or any typo like `--locale enUS`) produces garbage English-model output for non-English audio with zero indication anything was wrong. For an explicit user-supplied flag this is a quiet-wrong-answer bug rather than a graceful fallback (the app's engine sharing this mirror at least constrains locales via its language picker; the CLI accepts arbitrary strings).
evidence: if let enUS = await SpeechTranscriber.supportedLocale(equivalentTo: Locale(identifier: "en-US")) { resolvedLocale = enUS; return enUS }
proposed_fix: Expose the resolution: give FileTranscriber a `resolvedLocaleIdentifier()` (or make prepare() return the resolved Locale), and in runTranscribe/runDictate compare it against args.locale — when they differ, print a stderr warning: "warning: locale '<requested>' is not supported on this Mac; using <resolved>" (or exit 1 for an explicit mismatch, matching the CLI's honest-errors posture).

title: Launch-at-login registration failures are swallowed and the persisted toggle never reconciles with SMAppService status
description: LaunchAtLogin.set catches SMAppService register/unregister errors and only NSLogs. AppSettings.launchAtLogin's didSet (AppSettings.swift:359-362) persists the boolean to UserDefaults BEFORE calling LaunchAtLogin.set, so when registration fails (app running from a translocated/quarantined location, a dev build outside /Applications, or SMAppService .requiresApproval where the user must approve in System Settings ▸ Login Items) the Settings toggle — and the H8 earned offer's "Talkie will start at login." confirmation (AppDelegate.swift:2898) — show ON while no login item exists. The reverse drift also never heals: if the user removes the login item in System Settings, `SMAppService.mainApp.status` is no longer .enabled but the persisted setting stays true forever (nothing reads LaunchAtLogin.isEnabled at launch), so the UI, the H8 gate (`shouldOffer(launchAtLogin:)`) and the BugBundle diagnostic all report a state that's false on the machine.
evidence: } catch { NSLog("Talkie: launch-at-login change failed: \(error.localizedDescription)") }
proposed_fix: (1) Make LaunchAtLogin.set return Bool (or throw) and, in AppSettings.launchAtLogin's didSet, revert the property/UserDefaults when registration fails, and when status == .requiresApproval surface SMAppService.openSystemSettingsLoginItems(). (2) At launch (applicationDidFinishLaunching), reconcile: if settings.launchAtLogin != LaunchAtLogin.isEnabled, update the stored setting to the real SMAppService state so UI/offer/diagnostics never lie.

title: MCP server silently drops malformed JSON-RPC requests instead of returning -32700 Parse Error
description: The stdio loop `continue`s without any response when a line fails JSON parsing (or isn't an object), and also silently drops a response that fails to re-serialize. JSON-RPC 2.0 requires a `{"error":{"code":-32700,…},"id":null}` response for parse errors; a host that sent a request it believes is valid (e.g. one that split a long message differently, or included a BOM/partial line) gets no reply at all and stalls until its per-request timeout, which surfaces to the user as a hung/flaky Talkie MCP tool call rather than an actionable error.
evidence: guard !trimmed.isEmpty, let data = trimmed.data(using: .utf8), let obj = try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: data) as? [String: Any] else { continue }
proposed_fix: On JSON parse failure for a non-empty line, print a JSON-RPC error response: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32700,"message":"Parse error"}}` and fflush(stdout), then continue. Keep the empty-line skip as-is.

title: retitle_meeting advertises a 'note' parameter in its schema but the handler silently discards it
description: The retitle_meeting tool spec (MCPServer.swift:225) documents a `note` property ("kept for the user's provenance"), but callTool invokes `store.queueRetitleMeeting(id: mid, title: title)` which takes no note, and TalkieStore.queueRetitleMeeting (TalkieStore.swift:164-171) hardcodes `note: nil` into the suggestion file. Every other mutating tool (add/remove/update vocabulary and replacement) threads `strArg("note")` through to the inbox file. A model that supplies the documented provenance note has it dropped on the floor, so the app-side confirmation loses the 'why' the schema promised the user would be kept.

proposed_fix: Add a `note: String?` parameter to TalkieStore.queueRetitleMeeting, pass it into the DictionarySuggestion (`note: note`), and call it from MCPServer with `note: strArg("note")` — matching the other five mutating tools.

title: StreamLanguageVoter.mergeWords is O(frames x words): multi-second CPU stall at meeting stop

That is seconds to tens of seconds of single-core CPU while the user waits in the 'isFinishing' state for their meeting note, and it grows quadratically with meeting length.

proposed_fix: Replace the inner full scan with an interval sweep: sort `valid` by start once, keep a cursor plus an active set (or a min-heap keyed by `end`) while walking frames in time order, so each word is added/removed exactly once. Complexity drops to O((frames + words) log words). Behavior is identical (same max-confidence-covering-midpoint winner).

title: talkieDebugLog does synchronous open/seek/write/close per message, unconditionally in release, with unbounded file growth
description: Every call opens /tmp/talkie-lang.log via FileHandle(forWritingTo:), seeks to end, writes, and closes — 3 syscalls + file-handle allocation per message. The file is never truncated or rotated, so an all-day dictation user accumulates transcript text in /tmp indefinitely. The header itself says 'TEMPORARY: remove once tuning is settled.'

title: TranscriptionEngine.conform builds a new AVAudioConverter per call — per chunk in file import, per buffer in multilang fanout
description: conform() constructs AVAudioConverter(from:to:) on every invocation when formats differ. FileImport.decodeAudioFile calls it once per ~1s chunk (3,600 converter constructions per hour of audio, FileImport.swift:337) and decodeVideo once per CMSampleBuffer (~0.1-0.2s of audio each → 20k-40k constructions per hour of video, FileImport.swift:393). MultiLangStreamTranscriber.fanout calls it per input buffer per lane (~12-94x/sec per stream, MultiLangStreamTranscriber.swift:313) — a hidden per-buffer converter construction whenever any lane's best format differs from the reference lane's. AVAudioConverter construction with rate conversion costs ~0.05-0.5ms plus allocator churn, and rebuilding it per chunk also discards resampler state between chunks.

proposed_fix: Add an overload of conform (or a small ConformingConverter class) that caches the AVAudioConverter keyed by (source format, target format) and is owned by the call site: one per Lane in MultiLangStreamTranscriber, one per decode loop in FileImportEngine.
