title: TalkieBridge (77 lines) is compiled into every default build's package graph but never linked, imported, or injectable — the 'Connected' flavor it exists for does not exist
description: TalkieBridge is the opt-in Claude API client (Sources/TalkieBridge/ClaudeBridge.swift — Anthropic Messages API via URLSession). Its own doc (ClaudeBridge.swift:3-5) claims it 'is compiled into the app only in an opt-in "connected" build flavor', and check-no-network.sh excludes it on the same premise ('injected only into the opt-in Talkie (Connected) flavor'). Neither claim is true today: Package.swift declares it as an unconditional bare `.target` (lines 92-98) with zero dependents — `swift build` compiles this URLSession code on EVERY default build (unlike TalkieUpdater, which is correctly gated behind the `devTools` env check at line 114). Nothing anywhere imports TalkieBridge, no adapter to the app's `Summarizer` protocol exists, and the `TALKIE_CONNECTED` compile flag that would activate PrivacyWall's connected branch (Sources/Talkie/Backends/PrivacyWall.swift:26) is never defined by any build path (grep: only PrivacyWall.swift references it).
evidence:
.target(
        name: "TalkieBridge",
        path: "Sources/TalkieBridge",  // unconditional — vs. `if devTools { targets.append(... TalkieUpdater ...) }`
proposed_fix: WIRE THE GATE (keep the module — it is feature-18 roadmap scaffolding, but make the documented flavor real): in Package.swift, mirror the TalkieUpdater pattern — `let connected = (ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["TALKIE_CONNECTED"]?.isEmpty == false)`, move the TalkieBridge `.target` inside `if connected { targets.append(...) }`, and add `.define("TALKIE_CONNECTED")` to `talkieSwiftSettings` plus `"TalkieBridge"` to `talkieDependencies` under that same condition. This makes ClaudeBridge.swift's and check-no-network.sh's 'opt-in flavor' claims true, stops compiling networked code in default builds, and gives PrivacyWall's `#if TALKIE_CONNECTED` branch a definition path. (Alternative if feature 18 is far off: delete the target declaration lines 89-98 and keep Sources/TalkieBridge as uncompiled reference — but gating is 5 lines and matches the existing TalkieUpdater precedent.)

title: Known suspect 'requiresNetwork dead enforcement' is now FIXED via PrivacyWall — but 5 backend/summarizer instantiation sites still bypass the wall
description: Status update on the MVP-review finding: the enforcement is no longer dead. Sources/Talkie/Backends/PrivacyWall.swift now exists and `PrivacyWall.assertLocal(...)` is called at 7 composition sites (AppDelegate.swift:290 for TranscriptionEngine; OutputTranslator.swift:168, CommandRouter.swift:16, MeetingRecorder.swift:776, MeetingSubtopicEngine.swift:69, Niche/LLMJargonRepair.swift:36 for OnDeviceLLM), with unit tests in Tests/TalkieTests/PrivacyWallTests.swift. HOWEVER, five sites construct backends/summarizers WITHOUT the wall, weakening the documented contract ('the composition root must REFUSE any backend whose requiresNetwork is true'): AppDelegate.swift:1998 (`summarizer: OnDeviceLLM()` in the live command-dispatch path), CommandsView.swift:189 (`summarizer: OnDeviceLLM()` in the command try-out sheet), MeetingRecorder.swift:754 (`MeetingNotesFusion().fuse(... using: OnDeviceLLM())`), MeetingRecorder.swift:397 (`TranscriptionEngine(localeIdentifier: locale)` for the far-end lane), and Meetings/FileImport.swift:206 (`TranscriptionEngine(localeIdentifier: primaryLocale)`). Not a live leak (both conformers hard-code `requiresNetwork = false`), but the defense-in-depth is only as strong as its least-guarded instantiation site — a supply-chain/refactor swap at any of these five would skip the precondition entirely.
evidence: graph: self.contextGraph.snapshot(), summarizer: OnDeviceLLM()
proposed_fix: WIRE IT — one-line change per site: wrap each bare construction in the existing guard, e.g. `summarizer: PrivacyWall.assertLocal(OnDeviceLLM())` at AppDelegate.swift:1998 and CommandsView.swift:189; `using: PrivacyWall.assertLocal(OnDeviceLLM())` at MeetingRecorder.swift:754; `let far = PrivacyWall.assertLocal(TranscriptionEngine(localeIdentifier: locale))` at MeetingRecorder.swift:397; `let engine = PrivacyWall.assertLocal(TranscriptionEngine(localeIdentifier: primaryLocale))` at Meetings/FileImport.swift:206. `assertLocal` is a documented zero-cost pass-through that preserves the concrete type, so no other code changes.

title: ReplaceSelectionIntent is never constructed anywhere — the 're-dictate this selection' command (feature 12) is unreachable dead code
description: Grep across Sources/ and Tests/ finds zero `ReplaceSelectionIntent(` call sites. Its doc comment claims 'the router constructs it explicitly (edit-by-voice mode)' — but CommandRouter.intent(for:) (Sources/Talkie/Commands/CommandRouter.swift:46-88) has no such branch and no 'edit-by-voice mode' exists; the router only ever builds ScratchThatIntent, ReplaceWordIntent, MacroIntent, SpellingIntent, RunShortcutIntent, CrossSurfaceIntent, and RewriteIntent. Every other CommandIntent conformer is wired; this one has been orphaned since the router landed (commit 9ad16bb). It is also untested.
evidence:
struct ReplaceSelectionIntent: CommandIntent {
    let id = "replace-verbatim"  // doc: "the router constructs it explicitly (edit-by-voice mode)" — no such construction exists
proposed_fix: DELETE IT: remove Sources/Talkie/Commands/ReplaceSelectionIntent.swift (21 lines, no other references to update; git history preserves it if a future re-dictate-selection feature wants the shape back). Wiring it would require designing a whole new gesture/mode ('dictate over the current selection') that nothing else scaffolds — not a small wire.

title: DictationAssembler (58 lines) has zero references — superseded by StreamingCleanup
description: `grep -rw DictationAssembler Sources Tests` finds no instantiation, no property, no test — the only occurrences are its own declaration. It was added with the batched/streaming transcription feature (commit 4f5683e) and its role (clean finalized segments incrementally, join on stop) is now performed by `StreamingCleanup` (Sources/Talkie/StreamingCleanup.swift), which AppDelegate actually uses (AppDelegate.swift:229 `private var currentStreaming: StreamingCleanup?`, :1224 construction, :1723 `streaming.finishCleaned()`). An orphaned parallel implementation of a subtle concurrency pattern is a refactor trap — someone will 'fix' the wrong one.
evidence: final class DictationAssembler: @unchecked Sendable {  // zero call sites; StreamingCleanup is the live implementation
proposed_fix: DELETE IT: remove Sources/Talkie/DictationAssembler.swift entirely. No call sites to update; the build cannot break.

title: SubpagePlaceholder ('This settings page is coming soon.') is unused — all three L6 subpages shipped their real panes
description: The L6a scaffold placeholder view is referenced nowhere: the `navigationDestination` switch (SettingsView.swift:479-496) now resolves all three `SettingsPage` cases to real panes (AllLanguagesPage, MeetingsSettings, VerifyClaimsSubpage), each reachable via live NavigationLinks (LanguageSettings.swift:187, SettingsView.swift:432, PrivacySettings.swift:175). The placeholder struct and its user-facing 'coming soon' string (which also sits in the localization surface) are dead, and the stale scaffold comments at lines 61 ('until then they resolve to a placeholder') and 476-478 ('Each case resolves to a placeholder subpage for now') describe a state that no longer exists.
evidence: private struct SubpagePlaceholder: View {  // "nothing links to these routes yet" — false; all three destinations are real now
proposed_fix: DELETE IT: remove `SubpagePlaceholder` (SettingsView.swift:576-595) and update the two stale scaffold comments (lines ~57-62 and ~476-478) to say the three destinations are the shipped panes. Also drop the now-unreferenced 'This settings page is coming soon.' key from the localization catalog if it exists there.

title: VisualEffectView in DesignSystem.swift is unused and its doc claims a sidebar role it doesn't have
description: `VisualEffectView` (NSViewRepresentable wrapping NSVisualEffectView, DesignSystem.swift:293-310) has zero references anywhere in Sources/ or Tests/. Its doc comment says 'Used as the sidebar background so the desktop frosts through' — but the sidebar is a NavigationSplitView with its own Liquid Glass material (SettingsView.swift:170 comment: 'NavigationSplitView supplies the Liquid Glass sidebar'), and no view ever instantiates this wrapper.
evidence:
/// frosts through, exactly like a native Mac app.
struct VisualEffectView: NSViewRepresentable {  // zero uses
proposed_fix: DELETE IT: remove the `// MARK: - Native material` block, the doc comment, and the struct (DesignSystem.swift:288-310). Note the repo convention treats DesignSystem.swift as read-only for feature work (SettingsView.swift:554 comment), so land this as a deliberate cleanup commit, not a drive-by.

title: TranscriptionBackend seam is half-consumed: AppleSpeechBackend typealias, supportsContextualStrings, and the beginSession(onUpdate:onSegment:) overload have no production callers
description: The `TranscriptionBackend` protocol earns its keep through `requiresNetwork` (consumed by PrivacyWall.assertLocal at AppDelegate.swift:290). But three pieces of the seam are dead in production: the `typealias AppleSpeechBackend = TranscriptionEngine` (line 9) is referenced only in doc comments; `supportsContextualStrings` (line 13, protocol requirement at Protocols/TranscriptionBackend.swift:~17) is read by nothing — the app calls `setContextualStrings` unconditionally without consulting it (e.g. MeetingRecorder.swift:398); and the merged `beginSession(onUpdate:onSegment:)` overload (lines 18-24) has zero callers — AppDelegate uses the engine's native `beginSession(segmentHandler:)`/`setUpdateHandler` API directly. This is forward scaffolding for the second backend (feature 20 / the committed Windows sherpa-onnx plan), so full deletion fights the roadmap, but as shipped it is untested surface that can silently drift from the real call path.
evidence: typealias AppleSpeechBackend = TranscriptionEngine  // alias + supportsContextualStrings + beginSession(onUpdate:onSegment:) — no production callers
proposed_fix: TRIM, don't delete the seam: keep the `TranscriptionBackend` conformance and `requiresNetwork` (PrivacyWall depends on them), but remove the unused `typealias AppleSpeechBackend` (AppleSpeechBackend.swift:9), the `supportsContextualStrings` requirement (Protocols/TranscriptionBackend.swift and its implementations at AppleSpeechBackend.swift:13 and Tests/TalkieTests/PrivacyWallTests.swift:55), and the `beginSession(onUpdate:onSegment:)` overload (AppleSpeechBackend.swift:18-24) — reintroduce them in the PR that lands the second backend, when a caller exists to keep them honest. If the team prefers to keep the scaffold, at minimum fix the doc 'consumed by features 01 / 18 / 20' to say 'reserved for'.

title: SettingsRouter.pendingPage doc says 'nothing sets it yet' — but MeetingsView sets it; the stale comment invites deletion of live wiring
description: The comment on `pendingPage` (SettingsView.swift:77-81) reads 'Purely additive: nothing sets it yet' — written when L6c was future work. L6c has since shipped: MeetingsView.swift:341 assigns `router.pendingPage = .meetings` (the Meetings tab's deep link into the Meetings settings subpage), and SettingsHome drains it at SettingsView.swift:501-512. A maintainer trusting the comment could remove the drain (or the property) and silently break the deep link. Same-family note: `drainPendingPage`'s comment at line 507 ('nothing sets pendingPage until L6c') is equally stale.
evidence:
/// scaffold, consumed by L6c's Meetings deep link). Purely additive: nothing
/// sets it yet — vs. MeetingsView.swift:341: router.pendingPage = .meetings
proposed_fix: WIRE THE DOC to reality (comment-only edit): update SettingsView.swift:77-81 and :505-507 to say the Meetings tab's settings link (MeetingsView.swift:341) sets `pendingPage` and SettingsHome drains it on appear/change. No code change.

title: Theme.inkTertiary fails WCAG contrast for body-size text (2.6:1 light, 3.6:1 dark)
description: The tertiary ink token is used for real content text at 10–12pt all over the app — e.g. meeting row metadata (Sources/Talkie/MeetingsView.swift:583 '.foregroundStyle(Theme.inkTertiary)' on an 11pt eyebrow), segment timecodes (MeetingsView:937-938, 10pt monospaced), heatmap legend (DashboardView:1099). Light 0x969AA1 on surface 0xF5F6F8 is ~2.6:1; dark 0x70747B on 0x1B1B1E is ~3.6:1. Both are below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for small text, so timestamps, durations and captions are genuinely hard to read.
evidence: static let inkTertiary  = dyn(light: 0x969AA1, dark: 0x70747B)
proposed_fix: Darken/lighten the token itself so every call site inherits the fix: Theme.inkTertiary → dyn(light: 0x7A7E86, dark: 0x8A8E96) (~4.5:1 on Theme.surface in both modes). Alternatively keep the current value for purely decorative glyphs and introduce Theme.inkCaption at the AA-passing values, swapping it in wherever inkTertiary styles actual text (MeetingsView:583, 916, 938; DashboardView:1099).

title: Entire type system is fixed-size — ignores the system Text Size accessibility setting
description: All four typography tokens resolve to fixed point sizes ('.system(size: size, weight: weight)'), and 179 additional raw '.font(.system(size: N))' calls across 23 view files (HUD.swift alone has ~40) bypass even those tokens. Nothing in the app scales with the macOS accessibility text-size setting or Dynamic Type text styles. A handful of places DO use scaling styles (.callout at SettingsView:2492, .caption at SettingsView:2501, .headline in Niche/BiasABTestView.swift:44), so under a larger system text size those few strings grow while everything around them stays frozen — the worst of both worlds.
proposed_fix: Two steps: (1) mechanical — replace raw '.font(.system(size: N, weight: W))' with '.font(.talkieHeading(N, weight: W))' so all sizes route through the token layer (pure rename, no visual change); (2) make the token layer scale once: in TalkieFonts multiply size by NSFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle: .body).pointSize / 13 (or use Font.custom(_:size:relativeTo: .body) for the Young Serif faces) so the whole app follows the system text-size setting from one place.

title: Meeting pill ignores Increase Contrast / Reduce Transparency that the sibling HUD pill honors
description: MeetingPill is documented as 'a bigger sibling of the dictation HUD pill' reusing the same design language, but it hardcodes '.white.opacity(0.92)' / '.white.opacity(0.6)' / '.white.opacity(0.82)' and a 0.10 hairline (lines 63, 66, 78, 92) directly. The HUD deliberately funnels every white opacity through accessibility-aware helpers — HUD.swift:1011 'ink(_:)' lifts opacities to ≥0.95 under Increase Contrast and HUD.swift:1097-1100 turns the hairline into a full white ring. During a meeting (the pill is on screen for an hour) a high-contrast user gets the low-contrast washes the HUD explicitly protects against.
evidence: .foregroundStyle(.white.opacity(0.92))
proposed_fix: Port the HUD's pattern: give MeetingPillView the same highContrast/reduceTransparency inputs (NSWorkspace.shared.accessibilityDisplayShouldIncreaseContrast, as HUDModel does) and a local ink(_ opacity:) helper: .white.opacity(highContrast ? max(opacity, 0.95) : opacity); make the strokeBorder at line 92 use lineWidth 1.5 / opacity 0.9 under high contrast, matching HUD.swift:1098-1101.

title: HUD error state uses system .orange instead of the warning token — inconsistent within the same file
description: The '.error' pill's exclamation triangle is '.foregroundStyle(.orange)' — raw system orange — while the '.warning' pill 160 lines earlier (HUD.swift:1441) correctly uses '.foregroundStyle(Theme.featherGold)'. Two alert states on the app's single most-seen surface render in two different yellows, and system orange doesn't adapt with the feather palette's light/dark variants.
evidence: .foregroundStyle(.orange)
proposed_fix: Sources/Talkie/HUD.swift:1601: '.foregroundStyle(.orange)' → '.foregroundStyle(Theme.warning)' (alias of featherGold, matching line 1441). If error should read hotter than warning, use 'Theme.danger' (featherRed) instead — either way a Theme token, not .orange. Same one-line fix in Sources/Talkie/Niche/BiasABTestView.swift:73 if that dev screen is touched.

title: Two recording dots, two reds: MeetingsView uses Color.red while MeetingPill uses Theme.featherRed
description: The in-window RecordingDot fills with raw 'Color.red' (system red), while the notch pill's RecDot for the very same recording session fills with the brand token (Sources/Talkie/Meetings/MeetingPill.swift:109 '.fill(Theme.featherRed)'). During a meeting both indicators can be visible at once in visibly different reds (system red also shifts differently in dark mode than the macaw red 0xE0342B/0xF0473B).
evidence:
Circle()
            .fill(Color.red)
proposed_fix: Sources/Talkie/MeetingsView.swift:531: 'Color.red' → 'Theme.featherRed'. Consider also unifying the two dot implementations (12pt vs 9pt, different pulse curves) into one shared RecDot view in DesignSystem.swift since they signal the identical state.

title: Icon-only hover buttons have tooltips but no accessibilityLabel — and only appear on hover
description: The meeting-row actions are icon-only plain buttons with '.help()' tooltips but no '.accessibilityLabel': regenerate (line 592 '} label: { Image(systemName: "arrow.clockwise") }'), edit (line 600), copy (line 604), export menu (line 620), completion-dismiss xmark (lines 1218-1226). VoiceOver falls back to the SF Symbol's generic description, which doesn't go through the app's '.loc' pipeline (the app ships 10 languages). Same pattern at Sources/Talkie/DashboardView.swift:602-608 (banner xmark), Sources/Talkie/CommandsView.swift:247-253 (macro trash), Sources/Talkie/VibeCodingView.swift:144-150 (folder remove). Worse, the row buttons are gated on 'hovering' (line 588), so they're invisible to keyboard/VoiceOver users entirely. HUD.swift and ScratchpadCard.swift show the house style being violated — they label everything.
proposed_fix: Add '.accessibilityLabel("Regenerate summary".loc)' (and equivalents: "Edit transcript", "Copy transcript", "Export transcript", "Dismiss", "Delete this macro", "Remove this folder") next to each '.help()'. For the hover-gated group at MeetingsView:588, keep the visual hover reveal but don't remove the buttons from the hierarchy — render them with .opacity(hovering ? 1 : 0) so assistive tech can always reach them.

title: HUD pill radius 17 is a magic number repeated six times — no token
description: The pill's signature fixed corner radius (deliberately not a Capsule, per the comment at line 1083) is hardcoded as 17 at HUD.swift:1086, 1094, 1097, 1141, 1674 and 1676. It sits between Theme.Radius.control (13) and Theme.Radius.card (22) with no token, so the CountdownRing (1674/1676) and the pill background must stay manually in sync — a drift bug waiting to happen on the most-seen surface.
evidence: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 17, style: .continuous)
proposed_fix: Add 'static let pill: CGFloat = 17' to Theme.Radius in Sources/Talkie/DesignSystem.swift (with a doc comment: fixed HUD pill corner — never a Capsule, the pill grows downward) and replace all six literals with Theme.Radius.pill.

title: Near-miss corner radii (12, 10, 8) shadow the 13/9 tokens across Onboarding, Settings, Meetings
description: Theme.Radius defines control=13 and chip=9, but view code repeatedly uses off-by-one literals: OnboardingView:164/293/500/701 use 12, OnboardingView:617 uses 8, SettingsView:2447-2448 (relaunch warning banner) uses 12, MeetingsView:257 and 687 (notes/search wells) use 10, MeetingsView:950 uses 6. Ten '12's and assorted 10/8/6s sit one point off the tokens — invisible one-by-one, but it makes the corner language subtly incoherent between screens and makes a future radius change miss half the app.
evidence: .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous).fill(Theme.surface.opacity(0.55)))
proposed_fix: Snap to tokens: cornerRadius: 12 → Theme.Radius.control (OnboardingView:164, 165, 293, 294, 500, 501, 701, 702; SettingsView:2447, 2448); cornerRadius: 10 → Theme.Radius.chip or control (MeetingsView:257, 687 — pick one for both wells); cornerRadius: 8 → Theme.Radius.chip (OnboardingView:617, 618); cornerRadius: 6 → Theme.Radius.chip or keep for the tiny segment highlight (MeetingsView:950).

title: strokeBorder outlines contradict the documented 'never an outline (borderless)' v2 doctrine
description: DesignSystem.swift:8-9 declares 'Surfaces lift by contrast + one whisper shadow, never an outline (borderless)' and line 41 documents Theme.hairline as 'Row dividers only — never an element outline.' Yet onboarding outlines every inset panel with it (OnboardingView:165, 294, 501, 596, 618, 702 '.strokeBorder(Theme.hairline)'), and Settings does the same on the AllLanguagesTile (Settings/LanguageSettings.swift:210) and the relaunch banner (SettingsView:2448). Either these screens are off-doctrine, or the doctrine comment is stale — both are consistency bugs for the next contributor.
evidence: .overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 12, style: .continuous).strokeBorder(Theme.hairline))
proposed_fix: Decide once: (a) restyle these wells borderless — drop the .overlay(strokeBorder…) lines and rely on the Theme.surfaceSunken / surface.opacity fill contrast like the dashboard cards do; or (b) if outlines are wanted on translucent/glass contexts (onboarding sits over LiveBackground where fills go 0.55 opacity), amend the token doc at DesignSystem.swift:41 to '…and edge definition on translucent surfaces' so the exception is codified rather than drift.

title: Meeting consent banner's hardcoded white hairline vanishes in light mode
description: The banner card fills with '.regularMaterial' (adapts to light/dark) but strokes its edge with '.white.opacity(0.10)' — a dark-surface assumption copied from the HUD pill, which is legitimately always black. In light mode the white-on-white stroke disappears, losing exactly the edge definition the border exists to provide.
evidence: .strokeBorder(.white.opacity(0.10), lineWidth: 0.5)
proposed_fix: Replace '.white.opacity(0.10)' with 'Theme.hairline' (already appearance-adaptive: 0xE6E8EB light / 0x2B2B2F dark), or if a lighter specular edge is wanted keep it scheme-aware like GlassCard does (LiveBackground.swift:183 branches on colorScheme).

title: White-on-brand badges drop to ~2.8:1 in dark mode because the accent flips light
description: Theme.coral is 0x1F66B3 in light (white text on it ≈ 5.6:1, fine) but 0x4AA0E6 in dark — and the checkmark badge (LanguageSettings:173-175 'Image(systemName: "checkmark") … .foregroundStyle(.white)' on 'Circle().fill(Theme.coral)'), the bigger badge at LanguageSettings:330, and the numbered VerifyRow badge (Settings/PrivacySettings.swift:484-488) all keep hardcoded white foregrounds. White on 0x4AA0E6 is ~2.8:1, below even the 3:1 graphics threshold, so the selected-language checkmarks go mushy in dark mode.
evidence: .foregroundStyle(.white)
proposed_fix: Add an 'onBrand' ink token to Theme: 'static let onBrand = dyn(light: 0xFFFFFF, dark: 0x0E2233)' (dark ink on the light dark-mode accent, the same move Apple makes for tinted buttons), then replace '.foregroundStyle(.white)' at LanguageSettings.swift:175, LanguageSettings.swift:330 and PrivacySettings.swift:486 with '.foregroundStyle(Theme.onBrand)'.

title: BirdBuddy glow color is a hardcoded Color(red:…) outside the token system
description: The buddy's active glow is 'Color(red: 0.95, green: 0.45, blue: 0.13)' — the only raw RGB literal in any view file. The comment documents the hue choice as deliberate ('between the app's scarlet and gold, deliberately not the macaw blue'), which is fine, but the value lives outside Theme so it can't adapt light/dark and won't be found in a palette sweep.
evidence: private static let glowOrange = Color(red: 0.95, green: 0.45, blue: 0.13)
proposed_fix: Keep the hue, move the constant: add 'static let glowEmber = dyn(light: 0xF27321, dark: 0xF27321)' (0xF27321 ≈ the current 0.95/0.45/0.13) next to the feather palette in DesignSystem.swift, preserve the 'between scarlet and gold, deliberately not blue' comment there, and reference Theme.glowEmber from BirdBuddy.swift:193.

title: Page gutter '28' is repeated in 9 screens with no Theme.Space token
description: Every top-level page applies '.padding(28)' as its content gutter — DashboardView:127, SettingsView:472/1256/1799, MeetingsView:87, VibeCodingView:93, Memory/MemoryView.swift:65, Milestones/MilestonesView.swift:51, Diagnostics/SpeedDetailView.swift:47 — but Theme.Space only defines card(20)/gridGap(14)/section(24). The value is consistent today purely by copy-paste; it's the single most load-bearing spacing in the app and the only one without a token.
evidence: .padding(28)
proposed_fix: Add 'static let page: CGFloat = 28' to Theme.Space in Sources/Talkie/DesignSystem.swift and replace the nine '.padding(28)' literals with '.padding(Theme.Space.page)'.

title: BiasABTestView is the one screen styled like a different app (dev-only)
description: Answering the 'screens that feel like a different app' question: user-facing surfaces are impressively uniform; the only outlier is this Niche dev harness. It uses system text styles found almost nowhere else ('.font(.headline)' line 44, '.subheadline', '.caption'), raw '.orange' (line 73), and a plain '.stroke(Theme.hairline)' rounded rect (line 64) instead of talkieCard/SettingsCard. Since Niche is deliberately unwired from the live path (per project decision), this only matters if the screen ever ships; flagging so it isn't used as a copy-paste source.
evidence: .font(.headline)
proposed_fix: No urgency while dev-only. If it ever becomes user-visible: wrap sections in SettingsCard, replace .headline/.subheadline/.caption with .talkieHeading(15/13/11), '.orange' → Theme.warning, and the stroke-outlined TextEditor well with Theme.surfaceSunken fill at Theme.Radius.chip like MeetingsView:257.

title: HUD error 'No supported speech locale could be resolved.' is passive jargon with no next step
description: TalkieEngineError.noSupportedLocale surfaces verbatim in the HUD error pill (AppDelegate.swift:1325 and :1361 call hud.showError(error.localizedDescription)). 'Locale' and 'could be resolved' are developer-speak; the user gets no action to take. The string is also a bare literal — not wrapped in .loc and absent from Localizable.strings, so it never localizes.
evidence: return "No supported speech locale could be resolved."
proposed_fix: Replace with: "Dictation isn't available for your language on this Mac yet. Pick another language in Settings → Languages, then try again." — wrap all TalkieEngineError descriptions in .loc and add the new keys to Resources/Localizations/en.lproj/Localizable.strings (then ripple to the 9 other .lproj files).

title: HUD error 'The speech model could not be installed: %@' is passive and appends a raw system error
description: Shown in the HUD error pill on dictation-start failure. Passive voice ('could not be installed'), leaks a raw localizedDescription as the main clause, gives no recovery step, and is un-localized (no .loc).
evidence: return "The speech model could not be installed: \(detail)"
proposed_fix: Replace with: "Couldn't get the speech model — macOS downloads it once. Check your internet connection and free disk space, then try again. (%@)" — keep the system detail as a trailing parenthetical, wrap in .loc, add key to en.lproj Localizable.strings and ripple to the other 9 .lproj files.

title: HUD error 'No compatible audio format was found for the microphone.' is jargon with no next step
description: Surfaces in the HUD error pill when the mic can't feed the recognizer. 'Compatible audio format' means nothing to end users and there is no suggested action. Un-localized bare literal.
evidence: return "No compatible audio format was found for the microphone."
proposed_fix: Replace with: "Talkie couldn't get audio from that microphone. Pick a different mic under Settings → Input device, then try again." — wrap in .loc, add to en.lproj Localizable.strings, ripple to the other 9 .lproj files.

title: Two different phrasings for the same 'no on-device speech' condition
description: TalkieEngineError.transcriberUnavailable says "On-device speech recognition is not available on this Mac." while the canonical, already-localized string used by onboarding and AppDelegate.swift:1008 is "On-device speech isn't available on this Mac." (Resources/Localizations/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:591). Same condition, two registers — the stiff 'is not' variant wins in the HUD error path.
evidence: return "On-device speech recognition is not available on this Mac."
proposed_fix: Reuse the existing localized string: return "On-device speech isn't available on this Mac.".loc — one message for one condition, and it's already translated in all 10 .lproj files.

title: 'Couldn't save that note anywhere — nothing was typed, try again.' is confusing
description: Shown as a HUD error (AppDelegate.swift:1926) when the save-to-notes rescue fails. 'Nothing was typed' reads as if it's about the user's typing, when it means the note file wasn't written. The comma-spliced 'try again' feels tacked on.
evidence: "Couldn’t save that note anywhere — nothing was typed, try again."
proposed_fix: Replace value with: "Couldn't save that note — nothing was written to disk. Try again, or check where notes are saved in Settings → Notes & export." Update the same literal at Sources/Talkie/AppDelegate.swift:1926 and re-translate the key in the other 9 .lproj files.

title: Settings permission rows read like an OS spec and clash with the warmer onboarding copy
description: The Privacy & permissions rows say "Capture your voice while you dictate." (2397), "Detect your dictation key anywhere in the system." (2405), and "Paste the transcribed text into the app you're using." (2421). Onboarding phrases the same three permissions warmly ("To hear you while you dictate.", "To notice your one dictation key — nothing else you type.", "To place the finished text into the app you're using." — OnboardingView.swift:426/432/445). 'Capture', 'Detect', 'anywhere in the system', and 'the transcribed text' are robot-speak; 'transcribed text' also breaks the app-wide 'your words / your text' terminology.
evidence: detail: "Capture your voice while you dictate.",
proposed_fix: Align the three details with the onboarding voice: Microphone → "Hears you while you dictate."; Input Monitoring → "Notices your one dictation key — nothing else you type."; Accessibility → "Places your words into the app you're using." Add the three keys to en.lproj Localizable.strings (they are currently bare literals) and ripple translations.

title: 'optimistic' tag chip on the Dictation speed page is developer jargon
description: The last-dictations list tags a row "optimistic" (key at Resources/Localizations/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:577) when the optimistic-insert path ran. Users know this feature as 'Show your words the moment you stop' (Localizable.strings:717); 'optimistic' is internal vocabulary leaking into UI.
evidence: if record.optimistic { TagChip(text: "optimistic".loc, tint: Theme.featherPlum) }
proposed_fix: Rename the chip to "shown early" — change the key/value in en.lproj Localizable.strings:577 ("optimistic" → "shown early"), update the literal here, and re-translate in the other 9 .lproj files.

title: Calendar status 'Write-only — Talkie needs read access' uses API vocabulary and no fix path
description: macOS never shows users the phrase 'write-only'; the System Settings option is called 'Add Events Only'. The status also doesn't say where to fix it. Key exists at Resources/Localizations/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:743.
evidence: case .writeOnly: return "Write-only — Talkie needs read access".loc
proposed_fix: Replace with: "macOS granted add-only access — choose Full Access for Talkie in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Calendars." Update the key in en.lproj Localizable.strings:743 and ripple to the other 9 .lproj files.

title: CleanupEngine says 'smart cleanup' (term drift) and its worst case is a dead end
description: Everywhere else the feature is just 'cleanup' ('Cleanup & intelligence', 'cleanup style', 'cleanup pass'); only CleanupEngine.unavailableMessage (lines 186, 188, 190) calls it 'smart cleanup'. Line 190's "This Mac can't run on-device smart cleanup." also ends with no reassurance about what still works. These strings show on the Dictation speed diagnostics page (SpeedDetailView.swift:261) and are bare literals — not in Localizable.strings.
evidence: return "This Mac can't run on-device smart cleanup."
proposed_fix: In all three messages replace 'smart cleanup' with 'cleanup', and change line 190 to: "This Mac can't run on-device cleanup — your words still go in exactly as you said them." Wrap all three in .loc, add keys to en.lproj Localizable.strings, ripple translations.

title: Watched-folder card: 'Off.' sentence-opener and 'No folder — this feature is off' are robotic
description: The footer for the off state starts with the fragment "Off. Pick a folder and any audio or video file…" and the row value (line 404, key at Localizable.strings:543) reads "No folder — this feature is off" — 'this feature is off' is UI-spec voice, not Talkie's.
evidence: ? "Off. Pick a folder and any audio or video file that lands in it — an AirDropped voice memo, an iCloud recording — is transcribed into a note on your Mac, then moved into a “Transcribed” subfolder inside it. Talkie only reads local files and never opens a connection.".loc
proposed_fix: Footer: drop the 'Off.' prefix → "Not watching anything yet. Pick a folder and any audio or video file that lands in it — an AirDropped voice memo, an iCloud recording — is transcribed into a note on your Mac, then moved into a “Transcribed” subfolder inside it. Talkie only reads local files and never opens a connection." Row value (Localizable.strings:543): "No folder yet — Talkie isn't watching anything". Update both keys in en.lproj and ripple to the other 9 .lproj files.

title: 'median of your last dictation' — a median of one reads as nonsense
description: The n==1 branch of the Dictation speed card reuses 'median' phrasing for a single sample (key at Resources/Localizations/en.lproj/Localizable.strings:553). Honest-numbers is the brand; a one-item median undercuts it.

title: Dictation can start during MeetingRecorder.start()'s async window and both sessions stomp each other on the shared TranscriptionEngine
description: beginDictation() guards only `meetingRecorder?.isRecording != true, meetingRecorder?.isFinishing != true` (AppDelegate.swift:1014). But MeetingRecorder.start() sets `isRecording = true` only at the very end (MeetingRecorder.swift:460), after a long await window: `await AudioCapture.requestMicrophoneAccess()` (line 246, can block on a permission dialog), the calendar lookup (line 305), and `try await engine.beginSession(timedSegmentHandler:)` on the SHARED engine (line 343). MeetingRecorder tracks this window in a private `isStarting` flag (line 190) that AppDelegate cannot see. If the user presses the dictation hotkey while a meeting is spinning up (both flows are main-actor but interleave at suspension points), both call `engine.beginSession` on the shared TranscriptionEngine, whose exclusivity teardown (TranscriptionEngine.swift:357-364) silently cancels whichever session started first. Depending on ordering, the meeting's Me-stream dies (its mic audio feeds a cancelled analyzer's continuation forever), or the meeting's later `engine.finishSession()` at stop (MeetingRecorder.swift:668) finalizes the live dictation session mid-dictation. The reverse direction is guarded (start() checks isDictating/isProcessingDictation at line 241, and beginDictation sets isDictating=true synchronously), so only this direction is open.
evidence: guard meetingRecorder?.isRecording != true, meetingRecorder?.isFinishing != true else { … }  // vs MeetingRecorder: `isRecording = true` only at line 460, awaits at 246/305/343
proposed_fix: Expose the starting window from MeetingRecorder — e.g. make `isStarting` a `private(set) var` (or @Published) — and extend the guard in AppDelegate.beginDictation (line 1014) to `guard meetingRecorder?.isRecording != true, meetingRecorder?.isFinishing != true, meetingRecorder?.isStarting != true else { … }` with the same HUD error. Both are main-actor, so no locking is needed; the flag is already set/cleared correctly (set at MeetingRecorder.swift:242, cleared via defer at 244).

title: Abandoned dictation-begin task calls blanket engine.cancelSession(), killing the NEXT session's analyzer (fast press–release–press loses the whole utterance)
description: In the beginDictation setup Task, after `let session = try await engine.beginSession(...)` (AppDelegate.swift:1266) the code re-checks `guard self.isDictating, self.sessionID == myID else { streaming?.cancel(); await engine.cancelSession(); … }` (lines 1268-1272; same pattern in the catch path at 1316-1320 and 1326-1327). TranscriptionEngine.cancelSession() (TranscriptionEngine.swift:579-596) has no session ownership token — it cancels whatever session is CURRENT. Sequence: press (session 1, Task A suspends in engine.beginSession — model install/analyzer start takes hundreds of ms), release (endDictation: sessionLive=false path, isDictating=false, no cancel — it relies on Task A's guard), press again (sessionID=2, Task B enqueues engine.beginSession). B's beginSession is queued on the engine actor while A's is still executing, so B runs BEFORE A's later cancelSession can be enqueued: B's internal exclusivity teardown correctly retires session 1 and installs session 2 — then Task A resumes on the main actor, its guard fails (sessionID 1 != 2), and its `await engine.cancelSession()` destroys SESSION 2's analyzer/results task. Session 2 proceeds (its own guard passes), audio feeds a finished stream, the HUD shows listening, and finishSessionDetailed later returns "" — the user's speech is silently lost. The likely actor-job ordering is exactly the harmful one.
proposed_fix: Never blanket-cancel when superseded. At both abandoned-path sites (AppDelegate.swift:1268-1272 and 1316-1320/1326-1327), replace `await engine.cancelSession()` with `if self.sessionID == myID { await engine.cancelSession() }` — when a newer session took over (sessionID advanced), engine.beginSession's own exclusivity teardown (TranscriptionEngine.swift:357-364) has already retired the stale session, so skipping the cancel is correct. (A more robust variant: have beginSession return a session token and add `cancelSession(ifCurrent: token)` to TranscriptionEngine.)

title: MeetingAudioFileWriter has no 'closed' latch — a late mic-tap buffer arriving after close() re-creates the AVAudioFile and destroys the finished meeting audio
description: MeetingAudioFileWriter.close() runs `queue.sync { file = nil }` (MeetingRecorder.swift:72) and returns; append() (line 36) enqueues `queue.async { … if file == nil { file = try AVAudioFile(forWriting: url, …) } … }` (lines 39-50). There is no closed flag, so any append enqueued AFTER close()'s sync block re-creates the AVAudioFile at the same URL — `AVAudioFile(forWriting:)` truncates/overwrites, so the just-finalized .m4a is replaced by a file containing one ~85 ms buffer, and stop() has already recorded it in `Meeting.audioFiles` (close() returned true at line 75). The window is real on the mic side: MeetingRecorder.stop() calls `audio.stop()` then `closeAudioWriters(record: true)` (lines 626-632), but AudioCapture.stop() (AudioCapture.swift:344-362) only does removeTap/engine.stop with NO drain of an in-flight tap callback — unlike SystemAudioCapture, which explicitly drains with `ioQueue.sync {}` (SystemAudioCapture.swift:476) precisely because 'an in-flight I/O block can still be appending'. An in-flight AVAudioEngine tap block on its internal render-notification thread can still execute `onBuffer?(converted)` (AudioCapture.swift:239) → writer.append → queue.async after close()'s barrier. Two call sites: the tap block (AudioCapture.swift:223-242, audio thread) vs MeetingRecorder.stop() → close() (main actor). Also minor: close() reads `started && !failed` outside the queue (line 75), which the late append then mutates. Consequence: total loss of that meeting's kept audio (keep-audio D9 feature).
proposed_fix: Add `private var closed = false` to MeetingAudioFileWriter; set it inside close()'s `queue.sync { closed = true; file = nil }` and capture the return values there too (`let ok = queue.sync { closed = true; file = nil; return started && !failed }`); in append()'s block, `guard !closed, !failed else { return }` so a late buffer can never re-create the file. Optionally also fix the enabler: in AudioCapture.stop(), pause/drain the tap before returning (e.g. install a generation flag the tap block checks, or accept the writer latch as the single point of truth — the latch alone is sufficient).

title: MeetingRecorder.tick() can fire during stop()'s awaits and spawn an analyzer rotation that interleaves with finish() via actor reentrancy — worst case wedges isFinishing forever
description: tick() guards only `guard let startedAt else { return }` (MeetingRecorder.swift:537) — it never checks `isRecording`/`isFinishing`. stop() invalidates the timer before its awaits (line 621), but a tick Task already queued on the main actor (`Task { @MainActor in self?.tick() }`, line 462) can still run while stop() is suspended between `await rotationTask?.value` (line 653) and `startedAt = nil` (line 693) — e.g. during `await mic.finish(anchorLocale:)` (line 664), when `micMulti`/`farMulti` are still non-nil. If the 600 s rotation boundary (`elapsed - lastRotationElapsed >= Self.meetingRotationInterval`, line 561) is crossed at that tick, it spawns a NEW `rotationTask = Task { await far?.rotate(); await mic?.rotate() }` (line 565) that stop() never awaits (it already awaited the old one). rotate() and finish() then interleave on the MultiLangStreamTranscriber actor via reentrancy at suspension points: rotate() mutates the reference-type Lane's `analyzer/continuation/results` (MultiLangStreamTranscriber.swift:284-286) while finish() iterates the same lanes (lines 333-351). If rotate swaps a fresh generation into a lane after finish() has called that lane's `continuation.finish()` but before `await lane.results.value` (line 345), finish() awaits a NEW generation's results task whose input stream is never finished and whose analyzer is live — the results stream never terminates, stop() hangs forever, and the `defer { isFinishing = false }` never runs: dictation AND new meetings are permanently blocked until app restart (beginDictation's guard at AppDelegate.swift:1014 and MeetingRecorder.start()'s guard at line 238 both key off isFinishing). Milder outcomes leak live SpeechAnalyzers. Narrow window (one queued tick coinciding with a rotation boundary during a multilingual meeting's stop), but the blast radius is an app-wide wedge. Note: analyzer rotation itself is the deliberate ~30-min fix (guardrail 4) — this is a bug in its stop-time coordination, not a proposal to remove it.
proposed_fix: Add `guard isRecording else { return }` at the top of tick() (after the startedAt unwrap) in Sources/Talkie/MeetingRecorder.swift:537. stop() sets `isRecording = false` synchronously before any await (line 614), so a stale queued tick reliably no-ops; nothing else needs tick during stop (the partial flush is superseded by stop's own finalize path). Belt-and-braces: in stop(), after `await rotationTask?.value` (line 653), re-check `rotationTask` for a newer task and await it too, or set a `rotationsClosed` flag that tick checks before spawning.

title: HotKeyMonitor.stop() racing the tap thread's startup can re-enable the tap and leak the run-loop thread, delivering duplicate gesture edges
description: start() spawns the tap thread (HotKeyMonitor.swift:119-135) which runs TWO separate lock sections: it reads `self.tap` under lock (lines 123-125), then creates the run-loop source, then re-locks to set `runLoopSource`/`threadRunLoop` (lines 128-131), then calls `CGEvent.tapEnable(tap:enable:true)` and CFRunLoopRun. If stop() (main thread, lines 143-165) runs in the window between those two sections, stop reads `threadRunLoop == nil` (so CFRunLoopStop is never called) and disables the tap — then the thread resumes, overwrites `runLoopSource`/`threadRunLoop` with fresh values, RE-ENABLES the tap stop() just disabled, and enters CFRunLoopRun forever. Result: isStarted=false but a live listen-only tap plus a leaked thread; a subsequent start() creates a second tap whose events feed the same shared `gesture` machine (refcon → same instance) — every physical key edge is then delivered twice (two enabled taps, one handler), which can corrupt the hold/tap-tap gesture decisions (spurious begin/end/lock callbacks). Separately, `healthTimer` (line 55) is read/written in start()/stop() with no lock, and `deinit { stop() }` (line 72) can run on any thread. Window is tiny (stop immediately after start — e.g. rapid settings churn at launch), hence low severity.
evidence:
self.lock.lock()
self.runLoopSource = source
self.threadRunLoop = CFRunLoopGetCurrent()
self.lock.unlock()
…
CGEvent.tapEnable(tap: tap, enable: true)  // thread may run this AFTER stop() disabled the tap
proposed_fix: In the thread body's second critical section (HotKeyMonitor.swift:128-131), re-check liveness before committing: `self.lock.lock(); guard self.isStarted, self.tap != nil else { self.lock.unlock(); return }; self.runLoopSource = source; self.threadRunLoop = CFRunLoopGetCurrent(); self.lock.unlock()` — and only then add the source and enable the tap. This makes a concurrent stop() either be seen (thread bails, never enables) or be preceded by a valid threadRunLoop (stop's CFRunLoopStop works). Also move `healthTimer` under `lock` (or document/enforce main-thread-only and drop the deinit stop() to an assertion).

title: talkieDebugLog appends to /tmp/talkie-lang.log from many threads with no synchronization — concurrent writers interleave and clobber each other
description: talkieDebugLog (TranscriptionEngine.swift:8-18) opens a fresh FileHandle per call, seeks to end, and writes — with no lock or serial queue. It is called concurrently from the TranscriptionEngine actor's results tasks, MultiLangStreamTranscriber lane reader tasks (MultiLangStreamTranscriber.swift:116/127/304), the main actor (MeetingRecorder, AppDelegate), MusicController's private queue (MusicController.swift:106), and detached tasks (ClaudeTranscriptLearner.swift:295). Two concurrent callers can both seekToEnd() to the same offset and then write, so one message overwrites the other (lost/garbled diagnostics — this is the file used to debug the language-detect pipeline, so corrupted lines directly undermine the tool's purpose).
